No converse statement is present: the equality of the kernel with the sum of the reflection kernels is proved in both inclusions directly, not as a two-direction equivalence claim requiring a separate reverse obligation.

citations.quote:
Fix $e\ge2$ and keep all conventions of
[[def-the-level-one-vector-representation-its-affinization-and-energy-function]]:
the Cartan datum, the space $V_{\mathrm{aff}}=\bigoplus_{m\in\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q(q)u_m$
with $u_m=z^av_j$ ($m=j-ae$, $j\in\{1,\dots,e\}$), the operators
$K_h,E_i,F_i$, the classical weights $\lambda_j=\Lambda_j-\Lambda_{j-1}$, and the
fixed coproduct $\Delta(K_h)=K_h\otimes K_h$,
$\Delta(E_i)=E_i\otimes K_i^{-1}+1\otimes E_i$,
$\Delta(F_i)=F_i\otimes1+K_i\otimes F_i$ of
[[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]].
Put $Q:=q^2$ and $c:=Q-1$, and let $Y_j$ denote the operator "multiply the $j$-th
tensor factor by $z$", so that $Y_j$ is invertible with
$Y_ju_m=u_{m-e}$ in the $j$-th slot and different $Y_j$ commute.

**The affine Hecke algebra $\tilde H_N$.** For $N\ge1$, $\tilde H_N$ is the
unital $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra with generators $S_1,\dots,S_{N-1}$ and invertible
$Y_1^{\pm1},\dots,Y_N^{\pm1}$ subject to

$$S_i^2=(Q-1)S_i+Q,\qquad S_iS_{i+1}S_i=S_{i+1}S_iS_{i+1},\qquad S_iS_j=S_jS_i\quad(|i-j|\ge2),$$

$$Y_iY_j=Y_jY_i,\qquad S_iY_j=Y_jS_i\quad(j\notin\{i,i+1\}),\qquad S_iY_iS_i=QY_{i+1}.$$

The element $t_i:=-q^{-1}S_i$ then satisfies $(t_i-q^{-1})(t_i+q)=0$; for a
reduced word $w=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_k}\in S_N$ put $S_w:=S_{i_1}\cdots S_{i_k}$
and $A_N:=\sum_{w\in S_N}S_w$ (well defined by the braid relations).

**The two-vector operator and its extension.** On residue tensors
$v_j\otimes v_k$ ($j,k\in\{1,\dots,e\}$) set

$$S(v_j\otimes v_k)=\begin{cases}-q\,v_k\otimes v_j,&j<k,\\ -\,v_j\otimes v_j,&j=k,\\ -q\,v_k\otimes v_j+(Q-1)v_j\otimes v_k,&j>k.\end{cases}$$

For a Laurent monomial $f=Y_1^pY_2^q$ define, with $s(f):=Y_2^pY_1^q$ the
swap of the two loop variables,

$$S(f\,w):=s(f)\,S(w)+(1-Q)\,Y_2\,\frac{f-s(f)}{Y_1-Y_2}\,w\qquad(w\in V\otimes V),$$

and extend linearly; the quotient $(f-s(f))/(Y_1-Y_2)$ is a Laurent polynomial,
so $S$ is a well-defined linear endomorphism of $V_{\mathrm{aff}}\otimes V_{\mathrm{aff}}$.
On $V_{\mathrm{aff}}^{\otimes N}$ the generator $S_i$ acts by this operator on
the tensor factors $i,i+1$ and $Y_j$ acts on the $j$-th factor as above; this
defines the **affine Hecke action**. The whole action commutes with the derived quantum group $U_q'(\mathfrak g)$ (the generators $E_i,F_i$ and $K_h$ with $h$ in the span of the simple coroots). Each $S_i$, and therefore $A_N$, also preserves total loop degree and commutes with the full affine quantum-group action. The individual loops instead satisfy $K_dY_jK_d^{-1}=qY_j$. Products are composed as left operators; right-action notation reverses their order using the anti-involution fixing the generators.

Fix $e\ge2$ and keep all conventions of
[[def-the-level-one-vector-representation-its-affinization-and-energy-function]]:
the Cartan datum, the space $V_{\mathrm{aff}}=\bigoplus_{m\in\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q(q)u_m$
with $u_m=z^av_j$ ($m=j-ae$, $j\in\{1,\dots,e\}$), the operators
$K_h,E_i,F_i$, the classical weights $\lambda_j=\Lambda_j-\Lambda_{j-1}$, and the
fixed coproduct $\Delta(K_h)=K_h\otimes K_h$,
$\Delta(E_i)=E_i\otimes K_i^{-1}+1\otimes E_i$,
$\Delta(F_i)=F_i\otimes1+K_i\otimes F_i$ of
[[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]].
Put $Q:=q^2$ and $c:=Q-1$, and let $Y_j$ denote the operator "multiply the $j$-th
tensor factor by $z$", so that $Y_j$ is invertible with
$Y_ju_m=u_{m-e}$ in the $j$-th slot and different $Y_j$ commute.

**The affine Hecke algebra $\tilde H_N$.** For $N\ge1$, $\tilde H_N$ is the
unital $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra with generators $S_1,\dots,S_{N-1}$ and invertible
$Y_1^{\pm1},\dots,Y_N^{\pm1}$ subject to

$$S_i^2=(Q-1)S_i+Q,\qquad S_iS_{i+1}S_i=S_{i+1}S_iS_{i+1},\qquad S_iS_j=S_jS_i\quad(|i-j|\ge2),$$

$$Y_iY_j=Y_jY_i,\qquad S_iY_j=Y_jS_i\quad(j\notin\{i,i+1\}),\qquad S_iY_iS_i=QY_{i+1}.$$

The element $t_i:=-q^{-1}S_i$ then satisfies $(t_i-q^{-1})(t_i+q)=0$; for a
reduced word $w=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_k}\in S_N$ put $S_w:=S_{i_1}\cdots S_{i_k}$
and $A_N:=\sum_{w\in S_N}S_w$ (well defined by the braid relations).

**The two-vector operator and its extension.** On residue tensors
$v_j\otimes v_k$ ($j,k\in\{1,\dots,e\}$) set

$$S(v_j\otimes v_k)=\begin{cases}-q\,v_k\otimes v_j,&j<k,\\ -\,v_j\otimes v_j,&j=k,\\ -q\,v_k\otimes v_j+(Q-1)v_j\otimes v_k,&j>k.\end{cases}$$

For a Laurent monomial $f=Y_1^pY_2^q$ define, with $s(f):=Y_2^pY_1^q$ the
swap of the two loop variables,

$$S(f\,w):=s(f)\,S(w)+(1-Q)\,Y_2\,\frac{f-s(f)}{Y_1-Y_2}\,w\qquad(w\in V\otimes V),$$

and extend linearly; the quotient $(f-s(f))/(Y_1-Y_2)$ is a Laurent polynomial,
so $S$ is a well-defined linear endomorphism of $V_{\mathrm{aff}}\otimes V_{\mathrm{aff}}$.
On $V_{\mathrm{aff}}^{\otimes N}$ the generator $S_i$ acts by this operator on
the tensor factors $i,i+1$ and $Y_j$ acts on the $j$-th factor as above; this
defines the **affine Hecke action**. The whole action commutes with the derived quantum group $U_q'(\mathfrak g)$ (the generators $E_i,F_i$ and $K_h$ with $h$ in the span of the simple coroots). Each $S_i$, and therefore $A_N$, also preserves total loop degree and commutes with the full affine quantum-group action. The individual loops instead satisfy $K_dY_jK_d^{-1}=qY_j$. Products are composed as left operators; right-action notation reverses their order using the anti-involution fixing the generators.

Fix $e\ge2$ and let $(I,A,D,P,P^\vee,\alpha_i,h_i,\delta,d,c,q)$ be the cyclic
affine type $A$ Cartan datum of
[[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]], so $I=\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$ and
$q_i=q$ for all $i$. Choose once and for all the representatives
$j\in\{1,\dots,e\}$ of the residues of $I$, so that $j=e$ represents the residue
$0$; all indices $j-1$, $j+1$ below are read in this representative range.

**The derived vector module.** Put $P^\vee_{\mathrm{cl}}:=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z h_i$, and let $U_q'(\mathfrak g)$ denote the subalgebra of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ generated by $E_i,F_i,K_h$ with $h\in P^\vee_{\mathrm{cl}}$. Let $V:=\bigoplus_{j=1}^{e}\mathbb Q(q)v_j$ and
define $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear operators $K_h$ ($h\in P^\vee_{\mathrm{cl}}$), $E_i$, $F_i$
($i\in I$) on $V$ by

$$K_hv_j:=q^{\langle\Lambda_j-\Lambda_{j-1},h\rangle}v_j,\qquad E_iv_j:=\delta_{j\equiv i+1}\,v_{j-1},\qquad F_iv_j:=\delta_{j\equiv i}\,v_{j+1},$$

where $v_0:=v_e$ and $v_{e+1}:=v_1$ are read cyclically, and $\equiv$ refers to
the residues of $I$. The vector $v_j$ has **classical weight**
$\lambda_j^{\mathrm{cl}}\in P_{\mathrm{cl}}$, where $\lambda_j:=\Lambda_j-\Lambda_{j-1}\in P$ is the fixed representative used in the affinization, and **residue** $j\in I$. These operators give the derived $U_q'(\mathfrak g)$-action; no degree operator $K_d$ is part of this finite action.

**Affinization.** The **affinization** $V_{\mathrm{aff}}$ is the
$\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space with basis $\{u_m\}_{m\in\mathbb Z}$, identified
with $V\otimes\mathbb Q[z,z^{-1}]$ by $u_m:=z^av_j$ whenever
$m=j-ae$ with $j\in\{1,\dots,e\}$ and $a\in\mathbb Z$; this representation of
$m$ is unique. On this space the full affine operators $K_h$ ($h\in P^\vee$), $E_i,F_i$ are

$$K_hu_m:=q^{\langle\lambda_j+a\delta,h\rangle}u_m,\qquad E_iu_m:=\delta_{m\equiv i+1}\,u_{m-1},\qquad F_iu_m:=\delta_{m\equiv i}\,u_{m+1},$$

so that in the $z$-picture
$E_i(z^av_j)=\delta_{j\equiv i+1}z^{a+\delta_{i0}}v_{j-1}$ and
$F_i(z^av_j)=\delta_{j\equiv i}z^{a-\delta_{i0}}v_{j+1}$. We write
$\mathrm{wt}(u_m):=\lambda_j+a\delta\in P$ and $l(u_m):=ae-j=-m$; the
**ordinary order** is $u_m>u_n\iff m>n$.

**Crystal data.** Put $B:=\{b_1,\dots,b_e\}$, $B_{\mathrm{aff}}:=\{u_m\}_{m\in\mathbb Z}$,
and define partial operators $f_i,e_i$ on $B_{\mathrm{aff}}$ by
$f_iu_m:=u_{m+1}$ if $m\equiv i$ and $f_iu_m:=0$ otherwise, and
$e_iu_m:=u_{m-1}$ if $m\equiv i+1$ and $e_iu_m:=0$ otherwise. Let

$$\varepsilon_i(u_m):=\delta_{m\equiv i+1},\qquad \varphi_i(u_m):=\delta_{m\equiv i},\qquad \varepsilon(u_m):=\sum_i\varepsilon_i(u_m)\Lambda_i^{\mathrm{cl}},\qquad \varphi(u_m):=\sum_i\varphi_i(u_m)\Lambda_i^{\mathrm{cl}},$$

in $P_{\mathrm{cl}}$. On the finite set $B$ the same formulas apply through
$b_j\leftrightarrow v_j$, so that $f_ib_j=b_{j+1}$ if $j\equiv i$ and $0$
otherwise, and $e_ib_j=b_{j-1}$ if $j\equiv i+1$ and $0$ otherwise.

**The opposite channel and its energy.** On $B_{\mathrm{aff}}\otimes B_{\mathrm{aff}}$
use the tensor rule $\otimes_+$

$$f_i(x\otimes y):=\begin{cases}f_ix\otimes y,&\varepsilon_i(x)\ge\varphi_i(y),\\x\otimes f_iy,&\varepsilon_i(x)<\varphi_i(y),\end{cases}\qquad e_i(x\otimes y):=\begin{cases}e_ix\otimes y,&\varepsilon_i(x)>\varphi_i(y),\\x\otimes e_iy,&\varepsilon_i(x)\le\varphi_i(y),\end{cases}$$

and the **energy function**

$$H_{\mathrm{op}}(z^ab_j\otimes z^bb_k):=\chi(j>k)+b-a,\qquad \chi(j>k):=\begin{cases}1,&j>k,\\0,&j\le k,\end{cases}$$

for $a,b\in\mathbb Z$ and $j,k\in\{1,\dots,e\}$. For a fixed **charge**
$M\in\mathbb Z$ the **ground sequence** is $b^\circ_s:=u_{M-s}$ ($s\ge0$).

derivations.claim: If $l(ws_i)=l(w)+1$, the reduced-word definition gives $S_wS_i=S_{ws_i}$. If $l(ws_i)=l(w)-1$, put $u=ws_i$, so $S_w=S_uS_i$ and the quadratic relation gives $S_wS_i=Q S_u+(Q-1)S_w$. Thus each paired term satisfies $(S_u+S_{us_i})S_i=Q(S_u+S_{us_i})$ for $l(us_i)=l(u)+1$. Summing the disjoint pairs gives $A_NS_i=QA_N$; left pairing gives $S_iA_N=QA_N$. Hence $A_NS_w=Q^{l(w)}A_N$ and $A_N^2=C_NA_N$. Inserting the largest letter into a permutation in each of its $N$ positions gives $\sum_{w\in S_N}Q^{l(w)}=(1+Q+\cdots+Q^{N-1})\sum_{u\in S_{N-1}}Q^{l(u)}$, proving the product formula by induction. It is nonzero in $k$.

For $N=2$, the quadratic identity gives $\operatorname{im}(S-Q)\subseteq\ker(S+1)$, and on that kernel $S-Q=-(1+Q)I$, so equality holds. The original two-factor space is the direct sum of the $R$-blocks $R(v_j\otimes v_j)$ and $Ra_{jk}\oplus Rb_{jk}$ for $j<k$. They are preserved by $S$. Every symmetric $f$ commutes with $S$ by [F2]. The ring $R$ equals $B+Bx$: indeed $y=(x+y)-x$, $x^2=(x+y)x-xy$, $x^{-1}=y/(xy)$ and $y^{-1}=x/(xy)$ reduce every Laurent monomial to this form. The sum is direct, since applying $s$ to $f+gx=0$ with $f,g\in B$ and subtracting gives $g(x-y)=0$, hence $g=f=0$. This also identifies $B$ as the symmetric Laurent subring. Consequently it suffices to compute $S-Q$ on $w,xw$ in each residue block; no localization of the tensor space is taken.

Put $J=\sum_i\ker(S_i+1)$. If $(S_i+1)v=0$, then $(Q+1)A_Nv=A_N(S_i+1)v=0$, so $J\subseteq\ker A_N$. Also $(S_i+1)(S_i-Q)=0$, so $(S_i-Q)v\in J$ for every $v$. For any operator word $T_1\cdots T_d$ with each $T_r$ a simple $S_i$, the exact telescoping identity $T_1\cdots T_d-Q^d I=\sum_{r=1}^d Q^{r-1}(T_r-Q I)T_{r+1}\cdots T_d$ shows that $(S_w-Q^{l(w)}I)v\in J$: each summand has its leftmost factor $S_i-Q$ and hence its image in a local kernel. Thus $(A_N-C_N I)v\in J$. If $A_Nv=0$, this gives $C_Nv\in J$, and $C_N\ne0$ gives $v\in J$. Therefore $\ker A_N=J$.

Write $d_j=v_j\otimes v_j$, $h=h_{jk}$ and $h'=h'_{jk}$. Formula [F2] gives $(S-Q)d_j=-(Q+1)d_j$ and $(S-Q)xd_j=-Q(x+y)d_j$. For $j<k$, it gives $(S-Q)a_{jk}=-Qh$, $(S-Q)b_{jk}=-q h$, $(S-Q)xb_{jk}=-Qh'$, and $(S-Q)xa_{jk}=-Q((x+y)h-q^{-1}h')$. By step 1.2 these images generate the entire kernel over $B$, proving the displayed formula. The alternative $(S-Q)$ basis description follows from the same image equality and [F3]. Quantum-group stability follows from [F1], and symmetric-loop stability from [F2]. In particular the correct base vector is $a_{jk}+q^{-1}b_{jk}$; the vector $a_{jk}-q b_{jk}$ instead has eigenvalue $Q$.

Since $A_N^2=C_NA_N$, $P_N=C_N^{-1}A_N$ is idempotent. Every $v$ decomposes as $(v-P_Nv)+P_Nv$, and an element in both its kernel and image is zero. Its kernel and image are those of $A_N$, giving the direct sum. The map $[v]\mapsto A_Nv$ is well defined, injective and onto its image; it commutes with the quantum-group action by [F1]. On that image $A_N$ acts by $C_N$ and every $S_i$ acts by $Q$ by step 1.1. Equivalently, $(S_i-Q)v\in J=\ker A_N$ implies that each $S_i$ induces scalar $Q$ on the quotient.

Equal indices have $u_l\otimes u_l=(xy)^p d_j\in\ker(S+1)$, for $l=j-pe$. If $l<m$ have equal residue, write $l=j-pe$, $m=j-re$. Their symmetric pair is $(x^py^r+x^ry^p)d_j\in Bd_j$, giving ordinary antisymmetry for $b=0$. For distinct residues write $l=j-pe$, $m=k-re$ and $t=xy$. If $j<k$, then $a=p-r\ge0$ and $b=k-j$; the relation for $a=0$ is $t^r h_{jk}$, and for $a>0$ its four tensor terms are exactly $t^r(x^a+y^a)h_{jk}$. If $j>k$, use $a_{kj}=v_k\otimes v_j$, $b_{kj}=v_j\otimes v_k$; now $a=p-r-1\ge0$ and $b=e+k-j$. The relation for $a=0$ is $t^r h'_{kj}$, and for $a>0$ its four terms are exactly $t^r(x^a+y^a)h'_{kj}$. All these vectors lie in the complete kernel of step 2.2, proving precisely the three displayed cases. Moreover $B$ is spanned over $k$ by $t^r$ and $t^r(x^a+y^a)$ with $r\in\mathbb Z$, $a\ge1$: pair each Laurent monomial with its swap and factor their common smaller power. Thus these relations span the entire kernel described in step 2.2, including its diagonal blocks, and give the full quotient presentation. For $a>0,b>0$, $(l+ae,m-ae)=(m-b,l+b)$ is decreasing and both entries lie strictly between $l,m$; the reverse pair has positive gap $ae-b=(a-1)e+(e-b)<ae+b=m-l$, so repeated application terminates.

At $q=1$, formula [F2] loses its divided-difference correction and sends $f(v_j\otimes v_k)$ to $-s(f)(v_k\otimes v_j)$, so $S_i$ is the negative flip on the entire Laurent-loop tensor space. Accordingly $S_w=(-1)^{l(w)}w$, $A_N$ is the signed antisymmetrizer, $C_N=N!$, and the preceding paired-length and kernel arguments remain valid over $\mathbb Q$ since $N!$ and $2$ are nonzero. The local kernel is now the ordinary symmetric two-factor space, giving the usual exterior quotient. This proves every asserted kernel, splitting and straightening claim on the original tensor space.

boundaries.reason: The crystal is the explicit list of e basis vectors with e at least two and the affinized index set is Z, so neither is empty, and the tensor square used for connectedness is nonempty; no empty-set or empty-product boundary enters.

boundaries.evidence: Vanishing is verified rather than assumed: step 1.3 checks that the generators send each v_j to zero or to one basis vector and that divided powers of order at least two vanish, and step 1.2 closes the tensor square using the cases where one side's arrow is zero.

Level one is the load-bearing hypothesis: step 1.1 computes that every epsilon and phi value is a level-one dominant weight and that the two maps are bijections onto the level-one dominant weights, with the minimum set equal to the whole crystal.

The degenerate a=0 boundary of the affinized chart is the base of the lattice: step 2.1 defines the bar involution on the span of all loop shifts and checks it on the unshifted basis vectors as well as on every shifted one, including the two-color swap at e=2.

The extremal weights of the finite Weyl orbit are included: step 1.1 checks the bijection onto the level-one dominant weights at both boundary classes of the orbit, and the parametrization by loop exponent is single-valued at exponent zero.

The basis is given by the explicit assignment G(b_j)=v_j and the lattice by its displayed span, while the bar involution is defined by inverting q and fixing the basis; no selection is made, so the lower-basis package is choice-free. The Definition's displayed basis and span carry the whole construction.

boundaries.reason: The item states structural properties of a fixed crystal and a fixed basis; it asserts no biconditional, so there is no forward branch of an equivalence to discharge.
No converse implication appears: perfectness, connectedness and the lower-basis axioms are each verified in the numbered steps, and no if-and-only-if is claimed between them.

citations.quote:
Fix $e\ge2$ and let $(I,A,D,P,P^\vee,\alpha_i,h_i,\delta,d,c,q)$ be the cyclic
affine type $A$ Cartan datum of
[[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]], so $I=\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$ and
$q_i=q$ for all $i$. Choose once and for all the representatives
$j\in\{1,\dots,e\}$ of the residues of $I$, so that $j=e$ represents the residue
$0$; all indices $j-1$, $j+1$ below are read in this representative range.

**The derived vector module.** Put $P^\vee_{\mathrm{cl}}:=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z h_i$, and let $U_q'(\mathfrak g)$ denote the subalgebra of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ generated by $E_i,F_i,K_h$ with $h\in P^\vee_{\mathrm{cl}}$. Let $V:=\bigoplus_{j=1}^{e}\mathbb Q(q)v_j$ and
define $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear operators $K_h$ ($h\in P^\vee_{\mathrm{cl}}$), $E_i$, $F_i$
($i\in I$) on $V$ by

$$K_hv_j:=q^{\langle\Lambda_j-\Lambda_{j-1},h\rangle}v_j,\qquad E_iv_j:=\delta_{j\equiv i+1}\,v_{j-1},\qquad F_iv_j:=\delta_{j\equiv i}\,v_{j+1},$$

where $v_0:=v_e$ and $v_{e+1}:=v_1$ are read cyclically, and $\equiv$ refers to
the residues of $I$. The vector $v_j$ has **classical weight**
$\lambda_j^{\mathrm{cl}}\in P_{\mathrm{cl}}$, where $\lambda_j:=\Lambda_j-\Lambda_{j-1}\in P$ is the fixed representative used in the affinization, and **residue** $j\in I$. These operators give the derived $U_q'(\mathfrak g)$-action; no degree operator $K_d$ is part of this finite action.

**Affinization.** The **affinization** $V_{\mathrm{aff}}$ is the
$\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space with basis $\{u_m\}_{m\in\mathbb Z}$, identified
with $V\otimes\mathbb Q[z,z^{-1}]$ by $u_m:=z^av_j$ whenever
$m=j-ae$ with $j\in\{1,\dots,e\}$ and $a\in\mathbb Z$; this representation of
$m$ is unique. On this space the full affine operators $K_h$ ($h\in P^\vee$), $E_i,F_i$ are

$$K_hu_m:=q^{\langle\lambda_j+a\delta,h\rangle}u_m,\qquad E_iu_m:=\delta_{m\equiv i+1}\,u_{m-1},\qquad F_iu_m:=\delta_{m\equiv i}\,u_{m+1},$$

so that in the $z$-picture
$E_i(z^av_j)=\delta_{j\equiv i+1}z^{a+\delta_{i0}}v_{j-1}$ and
$F_i(z^av_j)=\delta_{j\equiv i}z^{a-\delta_{i0}}v_{j+1}$. We write
$\mathrm{wt}(u_m):=\lambda_j+a\delta\in P$ and $l(u_m):=ae-j=-m$; the
**ordinary order** is $u_m>u_n\iff m>n$.

**Crystal data.** Put $B:=\{b_1,\dots,b_e\}$, $B_{\mathrm{aff}}:=\{u_m\}_{m\in\mathbb Z}$,
and define partial operators $f_i,e_i$ on $B_{\mathrm{aff}}$ by
$f_iu_m:=u_{m+1}$ if $m\equiv i$ and $f_iu_m:=0$ otherwise, and
$e_iu_m:=u_{m-1}$ if $m\equiv i+1$ and $e_iu_m:=0$ otherwise. Let

$$\varepsilon_i(u_m):=\delta_{m\equiv i+1},\qquad \varphi_i(u_m):=\delta_{m\equiv i},\qquad \varepsilon(u_m):=\sum_i\varepsilon_i(u_m)\Lambda_i^{\mathrm{cl}},\qquad \varphi(u_m):=\sum_i\varphi_i(u_m)\Lambda_i^{\mathrm{cl}},$$

in $P_{\mathrm{cl}}$. On the finite set $B$ the same formulas apply through
$b_j\leftrightarrow v_j$, so that $f_ib_j=b_{j+1}$ if $j\equiv i$ and $0$
otherwise, and $e_ib_j=b_{j-1}$ if $j\equiv i+1$ and $0$ otherwise.

**The opposite channel and its energy.** On $B_{\mathrm{aff}}\otimes B_{\mathrm{aff}}$
use the tensor rule $\otimes_+$

$$f_i(x\otimes y):=\begin{cases}f_ix\otimes y,&\varepsilon_i(x)\ge\varphi_i(y),\\x\otimes f_iy,&\varepsilon_i(x)<\varphi_i(y),\end{cases}\qquad e_i(x\otimes y):=\begin{cases}e_ix\otimes y,&\varepsilon_i(x)>\varphi_i(y),\\x\otimes e_iy,&\varepsilon_i(x)\le\varphi_i(y),\end{cases}$$

and the **energy function**

$$H_{\mathrm{op}}(z^ab_j\otimes z^bb_k):=\chi(j>k)+b-a,\qquad \chi(j>k):=\begin{cases}1,&j>k,\\0,&j\le k,\end{cases}$$

for $a,b\in\mathbb Z$ and $j,k\in\{1,\dots,e\}$. For a fixed **charge**
$M\in\mathbb Z$ the **ground sequence** is $b^\circ_s:=u_{M-s}$ ($s\ge0$).

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$, an index $i\in I$, and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra and let $A_i$ be the subalgebra generated by $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$ ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]); write $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$ for the divided powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]].

(i) The assignment $e\mapsto E_i$, $f\mapsto F_i$, $k\mapsto K_i$, $k^{-1}\mapsto K_i^{-1}$ defines an algebra isomorphism from the standard rank-one algebra $\mathbb A$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$, presented by $e,f,k^{\pm1}$ with $kek^{-1}=q_i^2e$, $kfk^{-1}=q_i^{-2}f$ and $[e,f]=(k-k^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ onto $A_i$; the images of the monomials $F_i^aK_i^mE_i^b$ ($a,b\ge0$, $m\in\mathbb Z$) are linearly independent in $U_q(\mathfrak g)$, being images of the PBW monomials of the triangular decomposition ([[thm-triangular-decomposition-of-a-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]).

(ii) For all $a,b\ge0$, $K_iE_i^{(a)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{2a}E_i^{(a)}$ and $K_iF_i^{(b)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{-2b}F_i^{(b)}$, and for $b\ge1$ the divided powers satisfy the exact commutation formula
$$E_iF_i^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}E_i+\frac{F_i^{(b-1)}}{q_i^{b}-q_i^{-b}}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}\bigl(q_i^{-2s}K_i-q_i^{2s}K_i^{-1}\bigr);$$
iterating it computes $E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}$ as a finite sum of monomials $F_i^{(b-t)}K_i^{m}E_i^{(a-t)}$ ($0\le t\le\min(a,b)$) with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$.

(iii) For every $N\ge0$ there is a simple $A_i$-module $L_i(N)$ of dimension $N+1$: it is the quotient of the cyclic module $\widetilde M(N):=A_i/\bigl(A_iE_i+A_i(K_i-q_i^N)\bigr)$ by the submodule generated by $F_i^{(N+1)}w_N$, where $w_N$ is the image of $1$, with basis the images $v_t$ of $F_i^{(t)}w_N$, $0\le t\le N$, on which $K_iv_t=q_i^{N-2t}v_t$, $F_iv_t=[t+1]_iv_{t+1}$ and $E_iv_t=[N-t+1]_iv_{t-1}$ (with $v_{-1}=v_{N+1}=0$); $L_i(N)$ is the unique simple $A_i$-module generated by a vector $v\ne0$ with $E_iv=0$, $K_iv=q_i^Nv$ and $F_i^{N+1}v=0$.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. For $m\in\mathbb N$, define the **$q_i$-integer**

$$[m]_i:=\frac{q_i^m-q_i^{-m}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}},\qquad [0]_i:=0,$$

and the **$q_i$-factorial**

$$[m]_i!:=\prod_{k=1}^m[k]_i,\qquad [0]_i!:=1.$$

For $0\le r\le m$, define the **Gaussian binomial** $\binom{m}{r}_i:=[m]_i!/([r]_i![m-r]_i!)$, and set it to $0$ when $r<0$ or $r>m$. In the published one-parameter convention, write $\binom{m}{r}_t:=\binom{m}{r,m-r}_t$ for the two-part $q$-multinomial coefficient of [[def-q-integer-q-factorial-and-q-multinomial]].

For an element $x$ of a unital $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra and $m\ge0$, define its **divided power at $q_i$** by $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$, so $x^{(0)}=1$ and $x^{(1)}=x$.

The symmetric convention and the published asymmetric convention are related, for $m\ge0$ and $0\le r\le m$, by

$$[m]_i=q_i^{-(m-1)}[m]_{q_i^2},\qquad \binom{m}{r}_i=q_i^{-r(m-r)}\binom{m}{r}_{q_i^2}.$$

In particular $[m]_i$ is invariant under $q_i\mapsto q_i^{-1}$. These quantities depend on the symmetrizer only through $q_i=q^{d_i}$.

Let $(L,B)$ be a crystal basis of an integrable chosen $P$-graded type-1 module $M$ ([[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]) with the induced operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ on $L/qL$ ([[def-kashiwara-crystal-operators]]). For $b\in B$ write $\mathrm{wt}(b)=\mu$ when $b\in B_\mu$, and define
$$\varepsilon_i(b):=\max\{n\ge0:\tilde e_i^{\,n}b\neq0\},\qquad \varphi_i(b):=\max\{n\ge0:\tilde f_i^{\,n}b\neq0\}.$$
Then (see below) both numbers are finite and
$$\varphi_i(b)=\varepsilon_i(b)+\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(b)\rangle .$$
The top of the $i$-string through $b$ is the vertex $\tilde e_i^{\,\varepsilon_i(b)}b$, of weight $\mathrm{wt}(b)+\varepsilon_i(b)\alpha_i$; its highest rank-one integer is $\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(b)\rangle+2\varepsilon_i(b)=\varepsilon_i(b)+\varphi_i(b)$.

In the crystal graph of $(L,B)$ the arrows $b\to\tilde f_ib$ are the inverse raising edges: on an existing edge, $\varepsilon_i$ increases by $1$, $\varphi_i$ decreases by $1$ and the weight decreases by $\alpha_i$, and the $i$-chains of $B$ are the finite strings with $\varepsilon_i(b)+\varphi_i(b)+1$ vertices.

For a crystal basis of the negative half $U_q^-$ ([[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]]) one uses the same arrows and the same finite $\varepsilon_i$, but defines the **formal** $\varphi_i:=\varepsilon_i+\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}\rangle$ as an integer of the abstract root-graded crystal; it may be negative, and it is not the lowering-chain length. The actual lowering-chain length of a negative-half vertex is denoted $\ell_i^-$ and equals $+\infty$, because $\tilde f_i$ is injective there; the negative half is not asserted to be an integrable finite-string module. No choice principle is used.

derivations.claim: Perfectness of $B$ except connectedness. By [F1] every $\varepsilon(b_j)=\Lambda_{j-1}^{\mathrm{cl}}$ and $\varphi(b_j)=\Lambda_j^{\mathrm{cl}}$ has level one, and the two maps are bijections $\{1,\dots,e\}\to\{\Lambda_0^{\mathrm{cl}},\dots,\Lambda_{e-1}^{\mathrm{cl}}\}=(P_{\mathrm{cl}}^+)_1$ because both $j\mapsto\Lambda_j^{\mathrm{cl}}$ and $j\mapsto\Lambda_{j-1}^{\mathrm{cl}}$ run through the $e$ fundamental classes; hence $B_{\min}=\{b:\langle c,\varepsilon(b)\rangle=1\}=B$ and axiom (P3) holds. For (P1): the weights $\lambda_j$ of $V$ are pairwise distinct with multiplicity one by [F1], and the finite Weyl group of the subdiagram $I\setminus\{0\}$ acts transitively on them: its reflection $s_i$ exchanges $\lambda_i^{\mathrm{cl}}$ and $\lambda_{i+1}^{\mathrm{cl}}$ and fixes the others, so adjacent exchanges reach every weight, so they form the finite Weyl orbit of $\lambda^\circ$ with one-dimensional weight spaces, contained in its convex hull.

Connectedness of $B\otimes B$ for the fixed coproduct. Use the fixed strict-$f$/non-strict-$e$ tensor rule. For an off-diagonal pair $(b_a,b_b)$ take $i\equiv a-1$. Then $\varphi_i(b_a)=0$ and $\varepsilon_i(b_b)=0$, because $b\ne a$, so the non-strict tie makes $e_i$ act on the first factor and sends $b_a$ to $b_{a-1}$ with cyclic representatives. Repeat until the first factor equals the second; at most $e-1$ steps are needed. From $(b_j,b_j)$, $f_j$ acts first on the first factor since $1>0$, producing $(b_{j+1},b_j)$, then on the second factor since $0\le0$, producing $(b_{j+1},b_{j+1})$. Thus every pair is connected to a diagonal and all diagonals are mutually connected, proving (P2). No attempt to apply $e_b$ to an arbitrary $b_a$ is made.

Lower basis and separated charts of $V$. Define coefficient bar by $q\mapsto q^{-1}$ and $\bar v_j=v_j$. The matrices of $E_i,F_i$ have entries $0,1$, so $\overline{E_iv}=E_i\bar v$ and $\overline{F_iv}=F_i\bar v$; derived torals satisfy the corresponding bar-inverted toral identity. Put $V_A=\bigoplus_j A v_j$, $V_0=\bigoplus_j A_0v_j$ and $V_\infty=\bar V_0$. Their intersection is $\bigoplus_j\mathbb Z v_j$: coefficientwise an integral Laurent polynomial regular at both zero and infinity is an integer constant. Its residue map at zero is the basis map $v_j\mapsto v_j+qV_0$, giving the balanced integral lifts $G(b_j)=v_j$. For a fixed color the nontrivial string is $v_i,v_{i+1}$, with $F_iv_i=v_{i+1}$ and $E_iv_{i+1}=v_i$ and coefficients $1$. Every other vector is a singleton killed by both operators. Therefore the normalized Kashiwara operators have the same $0,1$ matrices on this basis and preserve the genuine local chart; their residue arrows are $e_i,f_i$ from [F1]. Also $E_i^2=F_i^2=0$, hence the divided operators of order at least two vanish. The positive integral chart $\bigoplus_j\mathbb Z[q]v_j$ is retained separately and is stable here because the matrices are $0,1$; it is not the local coefficient ring.

The affinized chart. Put $L_{\mathrm{aff}}:=\bigoplus_m A_0u_m$ and $G(z^ab_j)=z^av_j=u_{j-ae}$; extend the bar involution by $\overline z=z$. Then $\overline{\cdot}$ is semilinear with coefficient bar $q\mapsto q^{-1}$, fixes every $G(z^ab_j)$, and satisfies $\overline{E_iw}=E_i\overline w$, $\overline{F_iw}=F_i\overline w$ for $w\in V_{\mathrm{aff}}$: the only loop shift occurs for $i=0$, where $E_0(z^av_1)=z^{a+1}v_e$ and $\overline{z^{a+1}v_e}=z^{a+1}v_e=E_0\overline{z^av_1}$, and the remaining cases have coefficients in $\{0,1\}$. The weight of $G(z^ab_j)$ is $\Lambda_j-\Lambda_{j-1}+a\delta$, and the string bound of step 1.3 is unchanged because each $i$-orbit is either the same nontrivial two-vertex string shifted by loops or a frozen singleton. The finite module $V$ carries only the $P_{\mathrm{cl}}$-weights $\lambda_j$ and no dominant level-one highest weight vector, so it is a level-$0$ $U_q'(\mathfrak g)$-module and not a level-one $P$-graded highest weight module; the $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$, $A_0=\mathbb Q[q]_{(q)}$ and positive $\mathbb Z[q]$ charts are used separately and are not identified.

Conclusion. The level-$0$ vector module has the level-one perfect crystal $B=\{b_1,\dots,b_e\}$ with the explicit $\varepsilon,\varphi$, connected tensor square and $B_{\min}=B$; the basis $G(b_j)=v_j$ is a lower global basis of $V$ whose nontrivial $i$-strings have two vertices with coefficients $1$ and whose remaining color strings are frozen singletons and whose divided operators of order $\ge2$ vanish; and the affinized chart $G(z^ab_j)=z^av_j$ has the same properties with the full $P$-weight.

boundaries.evidence: The one-term boundary of the recursion is handled: the pair profile acts on unordered pairs, so a tuple of length at most one is already normal and the recursion performs no rewrite, and the spanning statement is made for every N at least 1.

Zero coefficients and zero corrections are handled: step 1.1's equal-residue case carries no correction terms, and step 2.1's fourth relation is applied only when both the quotient and the residue difference are positive, with the interior pair strictly between the endpoints.

The two unit coefficients are the cases of the displayed relations: the equal-residue case has coefficient -1 and the unequal-residue case has coefficient -q^{-1}, both appearing in step 1.1's case list, so the boundary coefficients are exhibited rather than generic.

The degenerate e=2 read of the gap is included: for e=2 the residue difference is 0 or 1 only, so the fourth relation is vacuous exactly when the two indices share a residue, which step 1.1 handles by the equal-residue case.

The recursion keeps every index inside the original extremes: step 3.1 proves each rewriting step preserves the index interval and strictly decreases the gap, so the outer endpoints of the pair are never passed.
The quotient, the two lattice charts and the rewriting rules are all defined by explicit spans and formulas, so the normal-ordering definition selects nothing.

The item's displayed energy criterion is used in its forward direction inside the rewrite: step 2.1 applies the three-term relation precisely for pairs whose opposite-channel energy is positive, and step 4.1 records the equivalence of the two formulations on the quotient.

The converse direction is the termination statement: step 3.1's well-founded gap measure shows every unordered pair is rewritten toward decreasing indices using only the cases of nonpositive energy, so no pair with decreasing indices is left unattended.

Let $k=\mathbb Q(q)$, $Q=q^2$, and let $M_N=V_{\mathrm{aff}}^{\otimes N}$ carry the action of
[[def-the-affine-hecke-algebra-action-on-finite-tensor-powers-of-the-vector-representation]].
Put $A_N=\sum_{w\in S_N}S_w$ and
$C_N=\sum_{w\in S_N}Q^{l(w)}=\prod_{r=1}^N(1+Q+\cdots+Q^{r-1})\ne0$.
Then:

(i) $A_NS_i=S_iA_N=QA_N$ and $A_N^2=C_NA_N$. The operator
$P_N=C_N^{-1}A_N$ is a $k$-linear idempotent commuting with the quantum-group action.

(ii) $\ker A_N=\sum_{i=1}^{N-1}\ker(S_i+1)$, a sum of $k$-subspaces, and
$M_N=\ker A_N\oplus\operatorname{im}A_N$. The map $[x]\mapsto A_Nx$ identifies
$M_N/\ker A_N$ with $\operatorname{im}A_N$ as quantum-group modules;
$A_N$ acts there by $C_N$, and every $S_i$ acts there by $Q$.

(iii) On two factors put $x=Y_1$, $y=Y_2$, $R=k[x^{\pm1},y^{\pm1}]$ and
$B=k[x+y,(xy)^{\pm1}]$, the symmetric Laurent subring. The complete partial
q-symmetric kernel on the original Laurent-loop vector space is
$$\ker(S+1)=\bigoplus_j B(v_j\otimes v_j)\ \oplus\!\bigoplus_{j<k}\left(Bh_{jk}+Bh'_{jk}\right),$$
where, writing $a_{jk}=v_j\otimes v_k$ and $b_{jk}=v_k\otimes v_j$,
$$h_{jk}=a_{jk}+q^{-1}b_{jk},\qquad h'_{jk}=x b_{jk}+q^{-1}y a_{jk}.$$
Equivalently, it is the $k$-span of $(S-Q)(u_l\otimes u_m)$ for all integers
$l,m$. This kernel is stable under the quantum-group action and symmetric
Laurent multiplication; arbitrary Laurent multiplication need not preserve it.
Its quotient satisfies the full local straightening relations: repeated entries
vanish, and for $l<m$, writing $m-l=ae+b$ with $a\ge0$ and $0\le b<e$,
$$u_l\wedge u_m=\begin{cases}-u_m\wedge u_l,&b=0,\\-q^{-1}u_m\wedge u_l,&a=0,\ b>0,\\-q^{-1}u_m\wedge u_l-u_{l+ae}\wedge u_{m-ae}-q^{-1}u_{m-ae}\wedge u_{l+ae},&a>0,\ b>0.\end{cases}$$
The remaining unordered pair in the third case has strictly smaller gap, so
repetition terminates. At $q=1$, $S_i$ specializes to the negative flip,
$A_N$ to $\sum_w(-1)^{l(w)}w$, and $C_N$ to $N!$; the kernel and quotient
are the ordinary local symmetric relations and exterior power.

Fix $e\ge2$ and keep all conventions of
[[def-the-level-one-vector-representation-its-affinization-and-energy-function]]:
the Cartan datum, the space $V_{\mathrm{aff}}=\bigoplus_{m\in\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q(q)u_m$
with $u_m=z^av_j$ ($m=j-ae$, $j\in\{1,\dots,e\}$), the operators

$$K_hu_m:=q^{\langle\lambda_j+a\delta,h\rangle}u_m,\qquad E_iu_m:=\delta_{m\equiv i+1}\,u_{m-1},\qquad F_iu_m:=\delta_{m\equiv i}\,u_{m+1},$$

$F_i(z^av_j)=\delta_{j\equiv i}z^{a-\delta_{i0}}v_{j+1}$. We write
$\mathrm{wt}(u_m):=\lambda_j+a\delta\in P$ and $l(u_m):=ae-j=-m$; the
**ordinary order** is $u_m>u_n\iff m>n$.

otherwise, and $e_ib_j=b_{j-1}$ if $j\equiv i+1$ and $0$ otherwise.

derivations.claim: Symmetric Laurent multiplication preserves $\ker(S+1)$. If $g=s(g)$, [F2] gives $S(gx)=gS(x)$, since the divided difference of $g$ is zero; this applies also to negative common loop shifts $(Y_1Y_2)^r$. On a diagonal $d_j=v_j\otimes v_j$ one has $S(d_j)=-d_j$. For $j<k$, set $w=v_j\otimes v_k$ and $w'=v_k\otimes v_j$; substitution gives $S(w+q^{-1}w')=-(w+q^{-1}w')$. For $j>k$ the divided differences of $Y_1,Y_2$ give $S(Y_1w)=-qY_2w'$ and $S(Y_2w')=-qY_1w+(Q-1)Y_2w'$, so $Y_1w+q^{-1}Y_2w'$ is a $-1$ eigenvector. These calculations take place in the original Laurent tensor space. Their images vanish in every adjacent pair of slots by [F1].

Diagonal and equal-residue relations. A repeated-index tensor is $(Y_1Y_2)^pd_j$ and hence vanishes. If $l<m$ have the same residue, write $l=j-(r+a)e$, $m=j-re$ with $a>0$. The symmetric multiple $(Y_1Y_2)^r(Y_1^a+Y_2^a)d_j$ is in $\ker(S+1)$ by step 1.1; its image is $u_l\wedge u_m+u_m\wedge u_l$, giving the equal-residue relation. No individual nonsymmetric loop multiplier of a kernel vector has been assumed to preserve the kernel.

Distinct residues without wrapping. Write $l=j-pe$, $m=k-re$ with $j<k$. Then $m-l=(p-r)e+(k-j)=ae+b$, so $p=r+a$ and $b=k-j$. If $a=0$, the symmetric common shift $(Y_1Y_2)^r(w+q^{-1}w')$ gives $u_l\wedge u_m=-q^{-1}u_m\wedge u_l$. If $a>0$, multiply the same kernel vector by the symmetric Laurent polynomial $(Y_1Y_2)^r(Y_1^a+Y_2^a)$. The four resulting images are, with coefficients $1,q^{-1},1,q^{-1}$, respectively $(l,m)$, $(m-ae,l+ae)$, $(l+ae,m-ae)$, $(m,l)$. Their sum is zero, which is precisely the fourth displayed relation.

Distinct residues across the representative boundary. If $j>k$, the same expressions have $p-r=a+1$ and $b=e+k-j$. The wrapped base kernel vector of step 1.1 is $h=Y_1w+q^{-1}Y_2w'$. For $a=0$, its common shift $(Y_1Y_2)^rh$ gives the third displayed relation. For $a>0$, its symmetric multiple $(Y_1Y_2)^r(Y_1^a+Y_2^a)h$ has images $(l,m)$, $(m,l)$, $(l+ae,m-ae)$ and $(m-ae,l+ae)$ with coefficients $1,q^{-1},1,q^{-1}$. Thus it gives the same fourth relation in this case also. Together with step 2.1 this exhausts all residue and Laurent-exponent configurations.

Pair recursion and whole-word termination. In the mixed case the correction indices are $m-b$ and $l+b$, strictly between $l$ and $m$, with gap $ae-b<ae+b$; the first correction pair is already decreasing, and the reverse pair can be rewritten recursively. For a word of length $N$, fix its original interval $[L,U]$ and total sum $T$. Every branch stays among the finitely many integer tuples in $[L,U]^N$ of sum $T$. Sort a tuple decreasingly and list its first $N-1$ prefix sums. Balancing a pair of extremes strictly decreases this list in lexicographic order: the sums of the largest $r$ coordinates cannot increase, and at least one decreases since the sorted multisets differ. A leading adjacent swap preserves this list and decreases by one the number of pairs of positions whose indices are increasing. Hence the lexicographic pair consisting of prefix-sum list and inversion count strictly decreases along each nonzero branch. Its range is finite, so rewriting terminates. Equal adjacent indices vanish; a terminal nonzero word is strictly decreasing.

Charts and energy. All coefficients in the displayed relations belong to $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$. Step 4.1 therefore expresses every Laurent tensor-lattice image in the $A$-span of the normal wedges; conversely each normal wedge is such an image. These two lattices equal $W_A$. Its positive chart is the separately defined $\mathbb Z[q]$-span $W_0$, and $q$ is a unit on $W_A$, so $W_A/qW_A=0$. The energy criterion is exactly [F3] and concerns the opposite channel. These computations establish every displayed relation and chart assertion in the Definition, using the kernel contract in [F1].

boundaries.reason: The two-factor module has an explicit basis indexed by the integers and the color set, so no empty tensor power or empty aggregate occurs, and the operators are all defined on this nonempty space.

boundaries.evidence: The symbolic denominator is a real obligation and is handled by expansion: step 1.1 defines the normalized operator through the geometric series in the ratio of loop variables and proves the cleared identity, so the zero locus is never inverted in the Laurent module.

The normalization constant is pinned by the cleared identity in step 1.1, and step 3.2 defines the flipped normalization with the stated leading behaviour, so the unit normalization of the braiding is computed rather than assumed.

The degenerate cases of equal indices and the two-cycle are covered: step 4.1 treats the equal-index tensors separately from the distinct-index ones, and the generation argument walks around the residue cycle, which at e=2 is the swap of the two colors.
The extremal diagonal is where the kernel lives: step 4.1 generates every base kernel vector from the orbit of the extremal diagonal and treats the equal-index tensor as its own endpoint case.

The normalized operator is defined by an explicit coefficient formula and the flip is the explicit factor swap; the kernel equality is proved by an algebraic identity, so nothing is selected. The Definition of the normalized operator is an explicit coefficient formula.

boundaries.reason: The item identifies operators and kernels by direct computation; beyond the definitional naming of the flipped operator it asserts no biconditional, so no forward branch of an equivalence is owed.
No converse implication is claimed: the statements are equalities of kernels and explicit properties of one normalized operator, so there is no reverse direction of an if-and-only-if.

derivations.claim: The left fraction and loop swap. From [F1], since $(a-1)Y_2=Y_1-Y_2$, the numerator simplifies as an operator to $(a-1)S+Q-1=[(a-1)S_0+Q-1]s$. Thus $R_{\mathrm{fix}}=R_0(a)s$ with $R_0(a)=((a-1)S_0+Q-1)/(Q-a)$, proving $R_{\mathrm{fix}}f=s(f)R_{\mathrm{fix}}$ for every Laurent loop function $f$. In particular it swaps $Y_1,Y_2$. All denominators are LEFT coefficients; no commutation of $S$ with $a$ is used. The inverse is $-a^{-1}\sum_{r\ge0}(Q/a)^r$, defined in the separated $q$-adic loop-module completion. For an extremal diagonal residue tensor $w$, $S_0w=-w$ and the numerator is $(Q-a)w$, so $R_{\mathrm{fix}}w=w$; common loop shifts give the same conclusion for each $u\otimes u$. By [F2] the original Hecke action and loop functions commute with $U_q'$; ratios have total degree zero, so the same operator intertwines the full affine action.

The exact original-space kernel. Subtracting the identity with LEFT denominator gives $R_{\mathrm{fix}}-1=(Q-a)^{-1}(a-1)(S+1)$. Multiplication on the left by $\psi_{\mathrm{fix}}=-(Q-a)/a$ gives exactly $(a^{-1}-1)(S+1)$. The formal $q$-adic coefficient $\psi_{\mathrm{fix}}$ is invertible, and multiplication by the nonzero Laurent polynomial $a^{-1}-1$ is injective on the original free Laurent-loop module by [F2]. Hence an ORIGINAL Laurent-loop vector is fixed by $R_{\mathrm{fix}}$ exactly when it lies in $\ker(S+1)$. No localization of the original kernel and no finite-dimensional weight-space assumption is needed.

Yang--Baxter. Use the FINITE residue operators $S_{0,1},S_{0,2}$ with commuting external variables $x,y$, and put $B_i(x)=(x-1)S_{0,i}+Q-1$. Expand $B_1(x)B_2(xy)B_1(y)$ and $B_2(y)B_1(xy)B_2(x)$. Reduce each square with $S_{0,i}^2=(Q-1)S_{0,i}+Q$ and each three-letter braid with $S_{0,1}S_{0,2}S_{0,1}=S_{0,2}S_{0,1}S_{0,2}$. The coefficients of the remaining Hecke words agree, using $(x-1)(y-1)+(x-1)+(y-1)=xy-1$ for the one-letter terms. The denominator is the common commuting product $(Q-x)(Q-xy)(Q-y)$. In step 1.1 the loop swaps supply precisely $x,y,xy$ on the three factors, so this finite-residue identity proves $R_{12}R_{23}R_{12}=R_{23}R_{12}R_{23}$ in the stated completion. It is not an expansion of full affine $S_i$ against noncommuting loop coefficients.

The opposite channel and its leading term. Define $R_{\mathrm{op}}=PR_{\mathrm{fix}}P$ with the full loop-and-factor flip. It intertwines the opposite coproduct because $P$ transports the checked fixed action, and its denominator is $1-Qa$. Evaluate $R_0(a)$ from step 1.1 on the three residue cases. At $q=0$ its pre-loop-swap factor is $a^{-1}$ for $j<k$, and $1$ for $j=k$ or $j>k$. Full flip exchanges both the residue order and $a$ with $a^{-1}$; hence the opposite pre-swap factors are $a,1,1$ for $j>k,j=k,j<k$. On $z^av_j\otimes z^bv_k$ the loop swap adds the exponent difference $b-a$, giving $H_{\mathrm{op}}=\chi(j>k)+b-a$ exactly as in [F3]. The opposite normalization and Yang--Baxter identities follow by the same full flip.

The full kernel generators. Step 2.1 and flip give $\ker(R_{\mathrm{op}}-1)=P\ker(S+1)$. The actual two-factor Laurent-loop kernel is generated over symmetric loop functions by the diagonal tensors and, for $j<k$, $h_{jk}=v_j\otimes v_k+q^{-1}v_k\otimes v_j$ and $h'_{jk}=Y_1v_k\otimes v_j+q^{-1}Y_2v_j\otimes v_k$ ([[lem-the-q-antisymmetrizer-determines-the-finite-q-wedge-kernel]]). Their flips, after multiplication by the units $q$ and $(Y_1Y_2)^{-1}$, are exactly the two order cases of the displayed $C_{j,k}$. Thus the displayed $C$ generate the entire original opposite kernel with symmetric loop shifts. To verify the full quantum orbit explicitly in the fixed channel, write $d_j=v_j\otimes v_j$. For $1\le j<e$, $\Delta F_jd_j=q h_{j,j+1}$ and $(\Delta F_j)^2d_j=(q+q^{-1})d_{j+1}$; hence all diagonals and all constant $h_{jk}$ are reached from $d_1$, extending the second index by the intervening finite lowering operators. Also $\Delta E_0d_1=Y_2(v_1\otimes v_e)+qY_1(v_e\otimes v_1)=q h'_{1e}$. For $j+1<k$, $\Delta F_jh'_{jk}=h'_{j+1,k}$, and for $j<k-1$, $\Delta E_{k-1}h'_{jk}=h'_{j,k-1}$; the partner factor has toral eigenvalue $1$ in both cases. These paths reach every $h'_{jk}$ with $j<k$, including $e=2$ where the first affine step already reaches the only such pair. Since symmetric Laurent multiplication commutes with the derived action, this proves that its symmetric-loop orbit contains the entire kernel basis. Conversely every such orbit element remains in the kernel by intertwining and symmetric-loop stability. Flipping proves the exact opposite quantum/symmetric-loop orbit asserted for the $C$ generators. Common loop shifts and symmetric powers produce every Laurent gap. This is the stated quantum AND symmetric-loop orbit, not arbitrary individual loop multiplication of a kernel vector. Flip back therefore gives precisely the full finite straightening quotient.

Conclusion. The checked completed left fraction swaps loops, fixes extremal diagonals, intertwines the fixed action and satisfies normalized Yang--Baxter. Its polynomial-cleared identity has injective Laurent multiplier on original vectors, giving the exact original-space kernel. The opposite flip has the stated energy, denominator and full symmetric-loop/quantum kernel generators, and transports back to the fixed finite-wedge quotient.

boundaries.reason: The theorem is stated for each fixed wedge length N at least 1 and the straightening profile is defined on tuples of that length, so no empty wedge enters and there is no empty-case obligation.

boundaries.evidence: The boundary where a correction vanishes is treated: step 2.1's profile records that a leading adjacent swap needs no correction term, and step 2.3's crystal analysis keeps the cases where an arrow is zero separate from the nonzero ones.

The base of the induction is the single leading term: step 1.1 produces coefficients in the Laurent ring whose leading term is the wedge itself, and step 3.1 exhibits the normal wedges as a free generating set with unimodular leading behaviour.

The degenerate adjacent-pair configuration anchors the profile: step 2.1 checks that a leading adjacent swap decreases the inversion count while a genuine correction strictly decreases dominance of the sorted index multiset, including the alternating pairs relevant at e=2 used in step 2.3.
Indices are kept inside their original bounds: step 2.1 has the multiset of indices fixed under every relation, so after straightening every index lies between the original minimum and maximum.

The basis consists of the explicit normally ordered wedges and the straightening procedure is deterministic, so the basis theorem selects nothing. The Statement's explicit wedges and the deterministic straightening are the whole input.

boundaries.reason: The claims are spanning, independence and a crystal statement, none of them phrased as a biconditional, so the forward axis carries no obligation.
There is no converse direction here: independence and spanning are each proved directly, in steps 2.2 and 1.1 respectively, and no equivalence between them is asserted.

For $N\ge1$ let $V_{\mathrm{aff}}^{\otimes N}$ carry the affine Hecke action and put
$W_N:=V_{\mathrm{aff}}^{\otimes N}\big/\ker A_N$, where $A_N=\sum_{w\in S_N}S_w$;
write $u_{m_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{m_N}$ for the image of the pure tensor, and let
$\wedge$ denote this product. Call an index tuple **normal** (or normally
ordered) if $m_1>m_2>\cdots>m_N$, and set $W_A:=\sum_{\text{normal }I}\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\,u_I$,
$W_0:=\bigoplus_{\text{normal }I}\mathbb Z[q]\,u_I$, where $u_I$ is the image of
the corresponding ordered wedge.

For $l<m$ write $m-l=ae+b$ with $a\ge0$, $0\le b<e$ (so $a=\lfloor(m-l)/e\rfloor$
and $b$ is the residue difference). The **normal-ordering relations** are:

$$u_l\wedge u_l=0;\qquad u_l\wedge u_m=-u_m\wedge u_l\quad(b=0);\qquad u_l\wedge u_m=-q^{-1}u_m\wedge u_l\quad(a=0,\ b>0);$$

$$u_l\wedge u_m=-q^{-1}u_m\wedge u_l-u_{l+ae}\wedge u_{m-ae}-q^{-1}u_{m-ae}\wedge u_{l+ae}\quad(a>0,\ b>0),$$

where the last line is to be read as a relation in $W_N$ and is applied
recursively to its two remaining unordered pairs; each recursion step strictly
decreases the gap of the unordered pair it rewrites and keeps every index
between $l$ and $m$, so the procedure terminates. The energy normal order is
the equivalent formulation through the opposite-channel energy:
$u_{m_1}\wedge u_{m_2}$ is rewritten toward decreasing indices by
$H_{\mathrm{op}}(u_{m_1}\otimes u_{m_2})>0\iff m_1>m_2$ of
[[def-the-level-one-vector-representation-its-affinization-and-energy-function]].

Let $k=\mathbb Q(q)$, $Q=q^2$, and let $M_N=V_{\mathrm{aff}}^{\otimes N}$ carry the action of
[[def-the-affine-hecke-algebra-action-on-finite-tensor-powers-of-the-vector-representation]].
Put $A_N=\sum_{w\in S_N}S_w$ and
$C_N=\sum_{w\in S_N}Q^{l(w)}=\prod_{r=1}^N(1+Q+\cdots+Q^{r-1})\ne0$.
Then:

(i) $A_NS_i=S_iA_N=QA_N$ and $A_N^2=C_NA_N$. The operator
$P_N=C_N^{-1}A_N$ is a $k$-linear idempotent commuting with the quantum-group action.

(ii) $\ker A_N=\sum_{i=1}^{N-1}\ker(S_i+1)$, a sum of $k$-subspaces, and
$M_N=\ker A_N\oplus\operatorname{im}A_N$. The map $[x]\mapsto A_Nx$ identifies
$M_N/\ker A_N$ with $\operatorname{im}A_N$ as quantum-group modules;
$A_N$ acts there by $C_N$, and every $S_i$ acts there by $Q$.

(iii) On two factors put $x=Y_1$, $y=Y_2$, $R=k[x^{\pm1},y^{\pm1}]$ and
$B=k[x+y,(xy)^{\pm1}]$, the symmetric Laurent subring. The complete partial
q-symmetric kernel on the original Laurent-loop vector space is
$$\ker(S+1)=\bigoplus_j B(v_j\otimes v_j)\ \oplus\!\bigoplus_{j<k}\left(Bh_{jk}+Bh'_{jk}\right),$$
where, writing $a_{jk}=v_j\otimes v_k$ and $b_{jk}=v_k\otimes v_j$,
$$h_{jk}=a_{jk}+q^{-1}b_{jk},\qquad h'_{jk}=x b_{jk}+q^{-1}y a_{jk}.$$
Equivalently, it is the $k$-span of $(S-Q)(u_l\otimes u_m)$ for all integers
$l,m$. This kernel is stable under the quantum-group action and symmetric
Laurent multiplication; arbitrary Laurent multiplication need not preserve it.
Its quotient satisfies the full local straightening relations: repeated entries
vanish, and for $l<m$, writing $m-l=ae+b$ with $a\ge0$ and $0\le b<e$,
$$u_l\wedge u_m=\begin{cases}-u_m\wedge u_l,&b=0,\\-q^{-1}u_m\wedge u_l,&a=0,\ b>0,\\-q^{-1}u_m\wedge u_l-u_{l+ae}\wedge u_{m-ae}-q^{-1}u_{m-ae}\wedge u_{l+ae},&a>0,\ b>0.\end{cases}$$
The remaining unordered pair in the third case has strictly smaller gap, so
repetition terminates. At $q=1$, $S_i$ specializes to the negative flip,
$A_N$ to $\sum_w(-1)^{l(w)}w$, and $C_N$ to $N!$; the kernel and quotient
are the ordinary local symmetric relations and exterior power.

Keep the conventions of
[[def-the-level-one-vector-representation-its-affinization-and-energy-function]].
Then:

(i) The derived level-$0$ module $V$ has **level-one perfect crystal**
$B=\{b_1,\dots,b_e\}$ in the sense of axioms (P1)-(P3): the weights of $V$ are
the finite Weyl orbit of $\lambda^\circ=\Lambda_1-\Lambda_0$ in $P_{\mathrm{cl}}$
with one-dimensional weight spaces, $B\otimes B$ is connected,
$\varepsilon(b)\in P_{\mathrm{cl}}^+$ and $\varphi(b)\in P_{\mathrm{cl}}^+$ have
level one for every $b$, the maps $\varepsilon,\varphi:B\to(P_{\mathrm{cl}}^+)_1$
are bijections onto the level-one dominant weights, and
$B_{\min}:=\{b:\langle c,\varepsilon(b)\rangle=1\}$ equals $B$.

(ii) The basis $G(b_j):=v_j$ is a **lower global basis** of $V$ for the ordinary
semilinear bar involution with coefficient bar $q\mapsto q^{-1}$ and
$\overline{v_j}=v_j$: the local $A_0$-lattice $V_0=\bigoplus_j A_0v_j$ is
bar-stable up to $q\mapsto q^{-1}$, the images $b_j=G(b_j)+qV_0$ are the
crystal elements, $\bar{E_iv}=E_i\bar v$ and $\bar{F_iv}=F_i\bar v$ for all
$v\in V$, all nontrivial rank-one strings have exactly two vertices with $E$- and
$F$-coefficients $1$, and all remaining color strings are frozen singletons, and the divided powers
$E_i^{(m)},F_i^{(m)}$ vanish for $m\ge2$. Here
$A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ and $A_0=\mathbb Q[q]_{(q)}$ are kept distinct, with the separate positive integral chart $\bigoplus_j\mathbb Z[q]v_j$. The Laurent, zero and infinity charts have balanced intersection $\bigoplus_j\mathbb Z v_j$, so this is the actual integral/bar-compatible lower basis.

(iii) The same statements hold on the affinization with
$G(z^ab_j)=z^av_j$, the loop variable fixed by the bar involution, and the full
$P$-weight $\Lambda_j-\Lambda_{j-1}+a\delta$; the finite $V$ is a
$U_q'(\mathfrak g)$-module with $P_{\mathrm{cl}}$-weights and is not a
level-one $P$-graded highest weight module.

Let $i\in I$, write $z=q_i$, and let $V(a)$, $V(b)$ be the simple rank-one modules of nonnegative integral highest weights $a,b$ for the subalgebra generated by $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$, with divided bases $v_j=F_i^{(j)}v_0$ $(0\le j\le a)$ and $w_k=F_i^{(k)}w_0$ $(0\le k\le b)$ ([[thm-quantized-sl-two-string-formulas]]). Consider the tensor product with the coproduct $\Delta E_i=E_i\otimes K_i^{-1}+1\otimes E_i$, $\Delta F_i=F_i\otimes1+K_i\otimes F_i$ ([[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]]), its Kashiwara operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ ([[thm-unique-kashiwara-i-string-decomposition]]) and the $\mathbb Z$-graded $\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space $V(a)\otimes V(b)$ with the tensor lattice
$$L:=\bigoplus_{j=0}^{a}\bigoplus_{k=0}^{b}A_0\,(v_j\otimes w_k)$$
over the local ring $A_0$ ([[def-the-local-ring-at-q-zero]]). Then:

(i) $L$ is a crystal lattice: it is a free $A_0$-module generating $V(a)\otimes V(b)$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$, it respects the weight grading, and $\tilde e_iL\subseteq L$, $\tilde f_iL\subseteq L$.

(ii) Modulo $q$ one has, for all $0\le j\le a$, $0\le k\le b$,
$$\tilde f_i(v_j\otimes w_k)=\begin{cases}v_{j+1}\otimes w_k & \text{if } a-j>k,\\ v_j\otimes w_{k+1} & \text{if } a-j\le k,\end{cases}$$
and
$$\tilde e_i(v_j\otimes w_k)=\begin{cases}v_{j-1}\otimes w_k & \text{if } a-j\ge k,\\ v_j\otimes w_{k-1} & \text{if } a-j<k,\end{cases}$$
where terms leaving the divided-basis ranges are $0$. In particular $\tilde f_ib=b'$ if and only if $b=\tilde e_ib'$ for residues $b,b'$ of the product basis (the partial-inverse property).

(iii) The nonzero residue strings are the chains $(0,t),(1,t),\dots,(a-t,t),(a-t,t+1),\dots,(a-t,b)$, $0\le t\le\min(a,b)$, and they partition the rectangle $0\le j\le a$, $0\le k\le b$.

This is a finite, choice-free calculation, independent of the grand loop and of global integral freeness.

derivations.claim: Spanning and termination. For any finite tensor combination choose a finite interval containing its indices. In each word the total sum stays fixed under [F1]. Among the finite set of words in this interval of that sum, order first the sorted decreasing prefix-sum list and then the increasing-pair inversion count. Each secondary balanced pair strictly decreases the former, while a leading adjacent swap decreases the latter and leaves the former fixed. The multiset can change in a secondary branch. Thus every branch terminates, either at zero from repeated adjacent indices or at a strictly decreasing tuple. The relations have coefficients in $A$, proving field spanning and Laurent spanning.

Field independence. For finitely many distinct normal tuples $I_k$, let $t_{I_k}$ be their raw tensors. Each $A_Nt_{I_k}$ is a finite Laurent-polynomial combination of raw tensors, regular at $q=1$. Select the finite union of all their supports as rows. At $q=1$, [F3] gives signed antisymmetrizations. The strictly decreasing raw row $t_{I_j}$ occurs with coefficient $1$ in column $j$ and coefficient $0$ in the other columns: distinct decreasing tuples have distinct index multisets. Therefore the square minor on these rows specializes to the identity determinant $1$ and is nonzero in $\mathbb Q(q)$. If $\sum_k c_k u_{I_k}=0$, [F2] gives $\sum_k c_k A_Nt_{I_k}=0$, so that nonzero minor forces every $c_k=0$. This proves field independence and, with step 1.1, a field basis for every $N$.

Laurent freeness. Step 1.1 supplies Laurent spanning. Any finite $A$-linear relation is also a field-linear relation and is zero coefficientwise by step 2.1. Thus the map from the direct sum of one copy of $A$ for each normal tuple to $W_A$ is both surjective and injective, proving precisely the claimed Laurent basis. No implication from torsionfreeness over a nonprincipal ring is used. The separate positive span is free over $\mathbb Z[q]$ by the same independence.

The exact rank-one cube. Fix a color $i$. The integer pairs $(i+ke,i+ke+1)$ are disjoint for every $e\ge2$. An empty pair is inert; a doubly occupied pair is inert because applying $E_i$ or $F_i$ makes a repeated adjacent index, whose wedge is zero. Its net $K_i$-weight is zero. A singly occupied pair is a copy of the highest-weight-one rank-one module. Changing a free bit shifts an index by one and keeps the word decreasing; the only possible obstruction is an already occupied partner, the frozen double-pair case. Hence each block of fixed pair occupancies is, in decreasing pair order, exactly a tensor product of these free rank-one modules. More explicitly, $F_i$ on a free high bit has coefficient $q^{\sum_{s<t}\epsilon_s}$ and $E_i$ on a free low bit has coefficient $q^{-\sum_{s>t}\epsilon_s}$, where $\epsilon_s=1$ for a high bit and $-1$ for a low bit and the sums are over earlier or later free pairs. Frozen pairs contribute zero. Thus the tensor cube identification is an equality of module actions.

Local crystal stability on every cube. Apply [F5] inductively to a cube with $r$ free pairs. For $r=0,1$ its divided-string basis is its ordinary basis. If the first $r-1$ factors have been written as a direct sum of simple divided strings with an $A_0$-basis whose residues permute the product basis, tensor each string with the final highest-weight-one factor. The finite calculation of [F5] produces a divided-string basis of each such tensor summand whose residues again permute its product residues. Its transition determinant is a unit of $A_0$, so the lattice remains exactly the $A_0$-span of the cube words, and the normalized operators act on these divided strings, preserve this lattice and permute its residues or send them to zero, with partial inverses. Induction proves these assertions for every finite cube. Step 3.2 identifies this lattice with the corresponding block of $L_0$; the block bases are subsets of the normal basis, and their direct sum covers every tuple. Consequently both normalized operators preserve $L_0$ and give the claimed crystal on its normal residues for every color.

The weight and integrability conditions. A normal wedge is a weight vector, since its raw tensor is one and the kernel is quantum-group stable by [F2]; thus the free local span decomposes by weights. It generates $W_N$ by step 2.1. For fixed color every tuple lies in the finite cube of step 3.2, a tensor product of finite rank-one modules; hence $E_i,F_i$ are locally nilpotent on all finite linear combinations. Together with the operator stability, residue basis and partial inverses of step 4.1, this proves that $L_0$ with the normal residues is a crystal basis of the integrable affine wedge module.

Conclusion. The normal wedges give the field and Laurent bases and the finite dominance termination profile; the exact rank-one cube action establishes the crystal basis on the separate local chart $L_0=A_0W_0$. The image of the positive tensor lattice is not identified with $W_0$ or $L_0$, and no triangularity of negative straightening powers at zero has been used.

boundaries.evidence: The direct limit is anchored at its extreme cases: step 1.1 stabilizes a finite word by appending a sufficiently deep tail and covers the case where there is nothing to append, and step 1.2 handles the empty partition as the vacuum word.

The q-adic neighbourhoods are the nonzero ideals generated by powers of q in the positive chart, and the zeroth power gives the chart itself: step 2.1 defines the topology by these neighbourhoods and separates it from the full Laurent chart.

The level-one normalization is fixed at the vacuum: the normalized vacuum weight is declared to be Lambda_0 of level one, and step 1.3 computes the recursion of consecutive vacuum weights with the explicit closed formula.

The apparent periodicity of the vacuum weight is a genuine boundary and is denied correctly: step 1.3 verifies the closed formula at the base parameter and records that no shift by the delta period reproduces the vacuum chain, so the degenerate-looking relation is not asserted.

Both ends of the limit are pinned: step 1.1 proves every finite word stabilizes along the appended ground tails, and step 1.2 proves the resulting normal words are exactly the partition-indexed ones, so the finite end and the stable end of the limit are both accounted for.

The limit is taken along the explicit ground tails and the basis is given by an explicit formula in the partition and the charge, so the construction selects nothing from a family. The Definition's explicit ground tails and basis formula carry the construction.

boundaries.reason: The item defines a space, a topology and a family of weights; it asserts no biconditional and therefore owes no forward branch of an equivalence.

No converse statement appears: the alternative description of the limit as a quotient of eventually-vacuum tensors is proved by direct comparison of the two constructions, not claimed as an if-and-only-if with a separate reverse obligation.

For every $N\ge1$ the normally ordered wedges
$\{u_{m_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{m_N}:m_1>m_2>\cdots>m_N\}$ of
[[def-finite-q-wedge-space-and-normal-ordering-relations]] form a
$\mathbb Q(q)$-basis of $W_N$ and an $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-basis of the
Laurent lattice $W_A$. The straightening algorithm terminates with a
well-founded profile: the total index sum and the ambient index interval are
preserved, secondary pairs become strictly more balanced in the sorted
dominance profile, and a leading adjacent swap decreases the inversion count;
in particular no bound by the initial inversion count alone is used. The
local $A_0$-chart $L_0:=A_0W_0$, where $A_0=\mathbb Q[q]_{(q)}$ and $W_0$
is the separate $\mathbb Z[q]$-span of the normal wedges, is a crystal basis: for each color $i$, on the occupied set of a normal tuple
the disjoint pairs $(u_{i+ke},u_{i+ke+1})$ behave as two-vertex highest-weight
$1$ strings, empty and doubly occupied pairs are frozen, and a shift of an
index by one either stays ordered or collides to zero; hence the residues of
the ordered wedges are stable under the normalized string operators and give a
crystal of the integrable affine wedge module. The image of the full
$\mathbb Z[q]$-tensor lattice need not equal $W_0$, and negative powers of $q$
in the straightening are not asserted to be triangular at $q=0$.

Fix $e\ge2$ and let $(I,A,D,P,P^\vee,\alpha_i,h_i,\delta,d,c,q)$ be the cyclic
affine type $A$ Cartan datum of
[[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]], so $I=\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$ and
$q_i=q$ for all $i$. Choose once and for all the representatives
$j\in\{1,\dots,e\}$ of the residues of $I$, so that $j=e$ represents the residue
$0$; all indices $j-1$, $j+1$ below are read in this representative range.

**The derived vector module.** Put $P^\vee_{\mathrm{cl}}:=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z h_i$, and let $U_q'(\mathfrak g)$ denote the subalgebra of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ generated by $E_i,F_i,K_h$ with $h\in P^\vee_{\mathrm{cl}}$. Let $V:=\bigoplus_{j=1}^{e}\mathbb Q(q)v_j$ and
define $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear operators $K_h$ ($h\in P^\vee_{\mathrm{cl}}$), $E_i$, $F_i$
($i\in I$) on $V$ by

$$K_hv_j:=q^{\langle\Lambda_j-\Lambda_{j-1},h\rangle}v_j,\qquad E_iv_j:=\delta_{j\equiv i+1}\,v_{j-1},\qquad F_iv_j:=\delta_{j\equiv i}\,v_{j+1},$$

where $v_0:=v_e$ and $v_{e+1}:=v_1$ are read cyclically, and $\equiv$ refers to
the residues of $I$. The vector $v_j$ has **classical weight**

in $P_{\mathrm{cl}}$. On the finite set $B$ the same formulas apply through
$b_j\leftrightarrow v_j$, so that $f_ib_j=b_{j+1}$ if $j\equiv i$ and $0$
otherwise, and $e_ib_j=b_{j-1}$ if $j\equiv i+1$ and $0$ otherwise.

$$H_{\mathrm{op}}(z^ab_j\otimes z^bb_k):=\chi(j>k)+b-a,\qquad \chi(j>k):=\begin{cases}1,&j>k,\\0,&j\le k,\end{cases}$$

derivations.claim: Finite-stage spanning and ordered-tail stabilization. Start with a finite word of length $r$ and choose $S\ge r$ so that the last appended ground index $L=M-S+1$ is below all its original indices. Its image at stage $S$ has $S$ entries, all at least $L$. By [F1], its finite straightening is a finite sum of normal tuples $n_1>\cdots>n_S\ge L$. For each resulting tuple put $\lambda_j=n_j-(M-j+1)$. Then $\lambda_S\ge0$ and $\lambda_j\ge\lambda_{j+1}$, so extending by zeros gives a partition. Every subsequent connecting map appends ground indices $M-S,M-S-1,\ldots$, strictly below the normal tuple's last entry; that image is already normal and is the longer prefix of the same partition word. Thus every direct-limit element is a finite combination of partition words with a stable representative under these ordered-tail extensions. Maps with different finite codomains are not equated.

Direct verification of the vacuum weights. Let $M=te+r$ with $t\in\mathbb Z$ and $0\le r<e$, and put $\Omega_M=\Lambda_r-[et(t-1)/2+tr]\delta$. It gives $\Omega_0=\Lambda_0$. If $r>0$, subtraction of the formula for $M-1=te+(r-1)$ gives $\Omega_M-\Omega_{M-1}=\Lambda_r-\Lambda_{r-1}-t\delta=\lambda_r-t\delta$. Here $u_M=z^{-t}v_r$, so this is exactly $\mathrm{wt}(u_M)$ by [F2]. If $r=0$, use $M-1=(t-1)e+(e-1)$: subtraction gives $\Omega_M-\Omega_{M-1}=\Lambda_0-\Lambda_{e-1}+(1-t)\delta=\lambda_e+(1-t)\delta$, and $u_M=z^{1-t}v_e$ has precisely this weight. These integer identities also hold for negative $t$. The base value and this recurrence uniquely determine the weights for all integer charges. The partition label is consequently the stipulated $\Omega_M-\sum_{\mathrm{cells}}\alpha_{c-r+M}$, whose $d$-evaluation is $\Omega_M(d)-m_0$ by the explicit datum; size remains the separate grading. No fractional change of an integer loop exponent or infinite unregularized weight sum is used.

Partition indexing and direct-limit independence. An eventually-ground normal word has $i_k=M+\lambda_k-k+1$ with $\lambda_k$ weakly decreasing and eventually zero; hence the $\lambda_k$ are nonnegative and form a partition, and every partition gives such a word. For finitely many distinct partitions choose a common prefix length $N$ containing all their nonzero rows and every position where two words differ. Each partition prefix is normal and has last index $i_N\ge M-N+1$. Its next appended index is $M-N$, strictly smaller, so every later image remains a normal basis word, and the distinct partition images remain distinct. If a finite linear combination vanished in the algebraic direct limit, it would vanish at some common later finite stage: a colimit relation uses finitely many connecting-map relations, which can all be moved to that common stage. Independence of the finite normal basis in [F1] then forces every coefficient to vanish. Together with step 1.1, this proves the partition basis without assuming that arbitrary finite words survive tail attachment.

The charts and the topology. Each displayed chart is free on the partition basis over its own ring. Both $F_A$ and $F_0$ contain $F_{\mathbb Z0}$, and $F_A\cap F_0=F_{\mathbb Z0}$ coefficientwise: an integral Laurent polynomial is regular at zero exactly when it has no negative powers. Neither chart is identified with the other. A nonzero vector of the local $A_0$-chart has finitely many nonzero coefficients, each of finite $q$-valuation, so $\bigcap_{n\ge0}q^nF_0=0$. On each finite label component the completion of $A_0=\mathbb Q[q]_{(q)}$ is $\mathbb Q[\![q]\!]$, and inverting $q$ gives the field completion $\mathbb Q((q))$; the corresponding full-field component is $\mathbb Q((q))\otimes_{\mathbb Q(q)}F^{(M)}_\mu$. Separately the completion of the integral $\mathbb Z[q]$-chart is $\mathbb Z[\![q]\!]$. The Laurent lattice has $qF_A=F_A$ and therefore supplies no separated $q$-adic filtration. These statements concern the componentwise completions stipulated in the Definition; no full infinite direct sum is identified with a finite-rank completed lattice.

Conclusion. The charge-$M$ Fock space is the algebraic direct limit of the finite wedge spaces along the ground tails, with a basis indexed by all partitions, the three charts $F_A,F_0,F_{\mathbb Z0}$ are distinct free lattices, the separated topology is induced by $q^nF_0$ (never by $q^nF_A$), and the vacuum weights are $\Omega_M=\Lambda_r-(\frac{et(t-1)}2+tr)\delta$ for $M=te+r$.

boundaries.reason: Every operator here acts on the fixed ground sequence and its finite prefixes, and the label-weight components are nonempty by construction, so no empty index set or empty aggregate arises.

boundaries.evidence: The zero cases are the content: step 1.1 shows the wedge with the filled tail is literally zero past a finite prefix, and step 3.1 shows the positive-size powers of the period operator vanish, so the geometric series is finite exactly because sufficiently high powers are zero.

The constant term and the single-insertion case are checked: step 2.2 treats one deep insertion of a loop-commuting endomorphism with its finitely many terms, and step 3.1's geometric series begins with the identity term.

The crossover where the power of the period operator first dies is treated: step 3.1 proves nilpotence on each positive-size component at the first power exceeding the size, and step 5.1 isolates the vacuum as the fixed case of the geometric sum.

The two tails are the two ends of the index line: step 1.1 treats the filled right tail, and step 2.1 obtains the dual left-tail statement by reversing the order of the indices, so both ends are covered.

The estimates are pointwise computations with explicit finite prefix lengths and powers, and the period operator is defined by an explicit shift, so nothing is selected from a family. The Statement's explicit ground sequence and period operator carry the whole computation.

dominance profile, and a leading adjacent swap decreases the inversion count;

$1$ strings, empty and doubly occupied pairs are frozen, and a shift of an
index by one either stays ordered or collides to zero; hence the residues of
the ordered wedges are stable under the normalized string operators and give a
crystal of the integrable affine wedge module. The image of the full

for $a,b\in\mathbb Z$ and $j,k\in\{1,\dots,e\}$. For a fixed **charge**
