On $V_{\mathrm{aff}}\otimes V_{\mathrm{aff}}$ put $a=Y_1/Y_2$ and let $P$ be the
flip of the two tensor factors including their loop variables. Define the
completed normalized left operator

$$R_{\mathrm{fix}}:=(q^2-a)^{-1}\bigl[(a-1)S+q^2-1\bigr],\qquad \psi_{\mathrm{fix}}:=1-q^2a^{-1},$$

where $S$ is the two-factor Hecke operator of
[[def-the-affine-hecke-algebra-action-on-finite-tensor-powers-of-the-vector-representation]]
and $(q^2-a)^{-1}$ is expanded $q$-adically as
$-a^{-1}\sum_{r\ge0}(q^2/a)^r$, so $\psi_{\mathrm{fix}}=1-q^2/a$ has constant term $1$. Then:

(i) $R_{\mathrm{fix}}$ swaps the two loop variables, fixes every extremal
pure tensor $u\otimes u$, and commutes with the fixed $U_q'(\mathfrak g)$-action;
the cleared identity
$\psi_{\mathrm{fix}}(R_{\mathrm{fix}}-1)=(a^{-1}-1)(S+1)$ holds in the Laurent
domain, and since multiplication by $a^{-1}-1$ is injective on the original
Laurent-loop module one has $\ker(R_{\mathrm{fix}}-1)=\ker(S+1)$ there, before
any localization.

(ii) $R_{\mathrm{fix}}$ satisfies the normalized Yang-Baxter equation
$R_{12}R_{23}R_{12}=R_{23}R_{12}R_{23}$ on the three-factor completed module.

(iii) The flipped operator $R_{\mathrm{op}}:=PR_{\mathrm{fix}}P$ with
$\psi_{\mathrm{op}}=1-q^2a$ is the opposite-channel ($\otimes_+$) normalized
braiding of
[[def-the-level-one-vector-representation-its-affinization-and-energy-function]]:
its $q^0$-leading term is
$z^{H_{\mathrm{op}}}b_1\otimes z^{-H_{\mathrm{op}}}b_2$ with the energy
$H_{\mathrm{op}}(z^ab_j\otimes z^bb_k)=\chi(j>k)+b-a$, and its kernel is
$N_{\mathrm{op}}=P\ker(S+1)$, the $U_q'(\mathfrak g)$- and symmetric-loop orbit of the extremal
diagonal generated by
$C_{j,k}=v_j\otimes z^{-\chi(j>k)}v_k+q\,z^{-\chi(j>k)}v_k\otimes v_j$ $(j\ne k)$
and $C_{j,j}=v_j\otimes v_j$. Flipping back gives the fixed-channel quotient
and the normal-ordering relations of
[[def-finite-q-wedge-space-and-normal-ordering-relations]].

Fix a **charge** $M\in\mathbb Z$ and let $W_N$ be the finite q-wedge spaces of
[[def-finite-q-wedge-space-and-normal-ordering-relations]]. For $r\le s$ define
the connecting map
$\varphi_{r,s}(u_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{i_r})
=u_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{i_r}\wedge u_{M-r}\wedge u_{M-r-1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{M-s+1}$,
so that new entries are the consecutive ground tail
$u_{M-N},u_{M-N-1},\dots$ appended to a prefix of length $N$. The **charge-$M$
Fock space** is the algebraic direct limit $F^{(M)}:=\varinjlim_{N}W_N$ of the
finite wedge spaces along these maps; equivalently it is the quotient of the
eventually-vacuum tensor space by the local wedge kernels. Write
$|\lambda;M\rangle$ for the image of the normally ordered semi-infinite word
with entries $i_k=M+\lambda_k-k+1$ indexed by the positive parts of the
partition $\lambda$, so that the vacuum $\varnothing$ corresponds to
$u_M\wedge u_{M-1}\wedge u_{M-2}\wedge\cdots$.

The **Laurent, positive and integral charts** of $F^{(M)}$ are

$$F_A:=\bigoplus_{\lambda}A\,|\lambda;M\rangle,\qquad F_0:=\bigoplus_{\lambda}A_0\,|\lambda;M\rangle,\qquad F_{\mathbb Z0}:=\bigoplus_{\lambda}\mathbb Z[q]\,|\lambda;M\rangle,\qquad A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}],\ A_0=\mathbb Q[q]_{(q)}.$$

The **separated q-adic topology** on the full field space is the one induced by
the filtration $q^nF_0$, never by $q^nF_A=F_A$; a finite $A_0$-label component
completes to a $\mathbb Q[\![q]\!]$-lattice, and the full-field component completes
to $\mathbb Q((q))\otimes_{\mathbb Q(q)}F^{(M)}_\mu$ for the label-weight
pieces. Separately, the integral $\mathbb Z[q]$-chart completes to a
$\mathbb Z[\![q]\!]$-lattice; this completion is not identified with
$\mathbb Q((q))$ and is not asserted to carry a $\mathbb Q$-vector-space
topology.

**Vacuum weights.** For $M=j-ae$ with $j\in\{1,\dots,e\}$ and $a\in\mathbb Z$
the vacuum $P$-weight $\Omega_M$ is normalised by $\Omega_0=\Lambda_0$ and
$\Omega_M-\Omega_{M-1}=\mathrm{wt}(u_M)$; explicitly, if $M=te+r$ with
$0\le r<e$, then

$$\Omega_M=\Lambda_r-\Bigl(\frac{e\,t(t-1)}{2}+tr\Bigr)\delta.$$

The weight of the partition $\lambda$ is
$\Omega_M-\sum_{\text{cells}}\alpha_{c-r+M}$, its size $|\lambda|$ is a separate
grading, and the $d$-eigenvalue is $\Omega_M(d)$ minus the number of residue-$0$
cells; no periodicity $\Omega_M=\Omega_{M-e}+\delta$ is asserted.

Fix an integer $e\ge 2$ and put $I:=\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z=\{0,1,\dots,e-1\}$
with its cyclic order; elements of $I$ are called **residues**. Let
$A=(a_{ij})_{i,j\in I}$ be the integer matrix with

$$a_{ii}=2,\qquad a_{i,i-1}=a_{i,i+1}=-1\ \ (i\in I)$$

when $e\ge 3$, and with $a_{00}=a_{11}=2$ and the single double edge
$a_{01}=a_{10}=-2$ when $e=2$; all indices are read modulo $e$. Thus for
$e\ge3$ all off-diagonal entries other than the neighbouring entries $-1$ are
$0$, and for $e=2$ the matrix is
$\begin{pmatrix}2&-2\\-2&2\end{pmatrix}$. Take the diagonal symmetrizer
$D=\operatorname{diag}(1,\dots,1)$ and the quantum parameter $q$ over
$\mathbb Q$, so that $q_i=q^{d_i}=q$ for every $i\in I$
([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]).

Choose free abelian groups

$$P=\Bigl(\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z\Lambda_i\Bigr)\oplus\mathbb Z\delta, \qquad P^{\vee}=\Bigl(\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z h_i\Bigr)\oplus\mathbb Z d,$$

with the $\mathbb Z$-bilinear pairing $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle:P\times
P^{\vee}\to\mathbb Z$ determined by

$$\langle\Lambda_j,h_i\rangle=\delta_{ij},\qquad \langle\delta,h_i\rangle=0,\qquad \langle\Lambda_j,d\rangle=0,\qquad \langle\delta,d\rangle=1 .$$

Define the **simple roots**

$$\alpha_i:=\sum_{j\in I}a_{ji}\Lambda_j+\delta_{i0}\,\delta\qquad(i\in I),$$

let $Q:=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z\alpha_i\subseteq P$ be the **root lattice**
and $Q^+$ its nonnegative cone, and define the **central element**
$c:=\sum_{i\in I}h_i\in P^{\vee}$. The **level** of $\lambda\in P$ is
$\langle c,\lambda\rangle\in\mathbb Z$ ([[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]),
and the **classical weight lattice** is $P_{\mathrm{cl}}:=P/\mathbb Z\delta$.

The **diagram reflection** $\tau$ is the pair of $\mathbb Z$-linear
involutions $\tau:P\to P$, $P^{\vee}\to P^{\vee}$ with
$\tau(\Lambda_i)=\Lambda_{-i}$, $\tau(\delta)=\delta$, $\tau(h_i)=h_{-i}$ and
$\tau(d)=d$ (indices negated in $\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$).

The **normalized affine weight form** is the symmetric $\mathbb Q$-bilinear form on $P_{\mathbb Q}:=P\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q$ determined, in the decomposition $P_{\mathbb Q}=Q_{\mathbb Q}\oplus\mathbb Q\Lambda_0$, by

$$(\alpha_i,\alpha_j)=a_{ij},\qquad (\Lambda_0,\alpha_i)=\delta_{i0},\qquad (\Lambda_0,\Lambda_0)=0.$$

Thus, for $x=\sum_i x_i\alpha_i$, $y=\sum_i y_i\alpha_i$ and $t,s\in\mathbb Q$, set

$$(x+t\Lambda_0,y+s\Lambda_0)=\sum_{i,j}x_i a_{ij}y_j+t y_0+s x_0.$$

In particular $(\lambda,\alpha_i)=\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle$ and $(\lambda,\delta)=\langle\lambda,c\rangle$. Its restriction to $Q$ is integer-valued; on all of $P$ it is rational-valued. This form on weights is distinct from the weight-coweight pairing. Define $s_i(\lambda):=\lambda-\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle\alpha_i$ and let $W$ be the group generated by these simple reflections; the form is $W$-invariant and $\tau$-invariant.

derivations.claim: Right-tail vanishing. Put $L=M-s$. By [F2], $H_{\mathrm{op}}(u_m\otimes u_L)\le0$ is equivalent to $m\le L$. Choose $B\le m$ and truncate the filled tail at $u_B$. The word $u_m\wedge u_L\wedge u_{L-1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_B$ has $L-B+2$ factors, all in the interval $[B,L]$, which contains only $L-B+1$ integers. Every normal term of its finite straightening would have that many distinct indices inside the same interval, which is impossible by [F1]. Thus this finite word is zero, as is every longer prefix. Its semi-infinite image is zero and therefore belongs to $q^nW_0$ for every $n$ at each such finite stage (and to $q^nF_0$ in the Fock space). This argument concerns the whole filled tail; it does not assert that $u_m\wedge u_L$ alone is zero when $m<L$.

Finite shifts of $C$. Here nonzero weight means that $C$ is homogeneous of a weight $\gamma
e0$: it maps a weight space of weight $
u$ into weight $
u+\gamma$. Write each $Cv_j$ as a finite sum $\sum_{k,a}c_{j,k,a}z^av_k$. Since $Cz=zC$ and $z$ is invertible, $C(z^tv_j)=\sum_{k,a}c_{j,k,a}z^{t+a}v_k$. Thus each term replaces $u_m$ by $u_{m+d}$, where $d=k-j-ae$ belongs to a fixed finite set obtained from the $e$ fundamental vectors; its coefficient depends only on $m mod e$. A term with $d=0$ would be the same vector $u_m$ and have weight shift zero, so its coefficient is zero by homogeneity. Choose $D$ bounding the absolute values of all occurring shifts.

Definition and gradings of $T$. On an eventually-ground word define $T$ by prepending $u_M\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{M-e+1}$ and replacing every old index $i_j$ by $i_j-e$. The simultaneous translation by $-e$ preserves the finite wedge relations: all residue differences and index gaps are unchanged. The new ground tail is again the charge-$M$ tail, so this operation respects local kernels and extending a representative by ground entries, and defines a linear endomorphism of $F^{(M)}$. At position $e+j$, its excess above the ground index is $(i_j-e)-(M-(e+j)+1)=i_j-(M-j+1)$; the prepended entries have excess zero. The old residues are unchanged by translation by $e$, and the new ground entries contribute zero residue-count deviation. Hence total size and label weight are preserved before and after straightening, by [F1] and [F3]. In particular $T$ preserves each label-weight/size component; this does not require a permutation of its partition labels.

Finite label weights. If $|\lambda;M\rangle$ has fixed label weight $\mu$, then $\Omega_M-\mu=\sum_i n_i\alpha_i$, where $n_i$ counts the residue-$i$ cells. Independence of the simple roots in [F3] uniquely determines all $n_i$ and hence $|\lambda|=\sum_i n_i$. Only finitely many partitions have this size: each has at most that many positive parts, each bounded by the size. Therefore each label weight contains finitely many partition basis vectors.

Dual left-tail vanishing. The mirrored filled tail ending at $u_L$ is $\cdots\wedge u_{L+2}\wedge u_{L+1}\wedge u_L$, with an extra factor $u_m$ on its right and the mirrored condition $H_{\mathrm{op}}(u_L\otimes u_m)\le0$, equivalently $m\ge L$. Truncate its left end at any $B\ge m$. The resulting word $u_B\wedge\cdots\wedge u_L\wedge u_m$ has $B-L+2$ factors inside the $B-L+1$ integers of $[L,B]$, so it is zero by the same finite normal-basis count. Extending that left end preserves zero. This is the reversed-interval version of step 1.1 and proves the dual exact finite vanishing and all its $q$-adic estimates.

Deep replacement. Fix an eventually-ground representative of a Fock vector. At a sufficiently deep slot its index is $m$, and the entire local block $u_{m+D}\wedge u_{m+D-1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{m-D}$ is ground. In a term of the insertion of $C$ at that slot, replace $u_m$ by $u_{m+d}$, where $0<|d|\le D$. This still has exactly $2D+1$ factors, all in $[m-D,m+D]$. Its total index sum is the ground block's sum plus $d$. By [F1] the only possible normal tuple of that cardinality in this interval is the complete ground tuple, whose sum is different. Every normal coefficient must therefore be zero. The block vanishes before it is wedged with the remaining factors, so the insertion is zero at every sufficiently deep slot; the cutoff is uniform for the finite shifts and, by taking a maximum, for any finite linear combination of representatives. These eventual zeros converge to zero in the separated $q$-adic topology.

Nilpotence on positive size. On $|\lambda;M\rangle$, $T^k$ prepends $ke$ ground entries and shifts all old indices down by $ke$. The largest shifted old index is $M+\lambda_1-ke$, so when $ke>\lambda_1$ all indices of the resulting word are at most $M$. Choose a finite prefix of length $R$ whose remainder is ground and whose last ground entry is below every nonground index. Its ground sum is $S_R=\sum_{j=1}^R(M-j+1)$ and its actual sum is $S_R+|\lambda|$, by step 1.3. Every normal $R$-tuple with maximum at most $M$ satisfies $a_j\le M-j+1$, and therefore has sum at most $S_R$. Straightening preserves sum and the upper bound $M$, so no such normal term exists if $|\lambda|>0$. Thus the finite prefix, and hence $T^k|\lambda;M\rangle$, is zero. Equivalently the only normal charge-$M$ semi-infinite word with maximum at most $M$ is the vacuum, excluded by the preserved positive size. Since $\lambda_1\le|\lambda|=n$, $T^k=0$ on the size-$n>0$ part whenever $ke>n$.

Geometric inverse. On a positive-size component choose $K$ with $Ke>n$. The finite operator sum $G=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}T^k$ satisfies $(1-T)G=G(1-T)=1-T^K=1$ by step 2.3. This gives the claimed finite geometric inverse on every nonvacuum label weight and the resulting isomorphism for the tail recurrence; no inverse on the vacuum component is asserted.

Conclusion. Steps 1.1 and 2.1 give the right and dual left filled-tail estimates by exact finite vanishing; step 2.2 gives eventual zero for every deep insertion of a loop-commuting homogeneous nonzero-weight endomorphism; steps 1.3, 2.3 and 3.1 give the size-preserving and label-weight-preserving period operator, its positive-size nilpotence bound and finite inverse; and step 1.4 proves finite label-weight components.

boundaries.evidence: The vacuum and the empty partition are the base of the bijection: step 1.1 includes the empty partition mapping to the ground word, and the node sums are finite because only boundary corners of the diagram contribute.
Zero terms are treated: steps 2.1 and 2.2 set the contribution to zero exactly on collisions, and step 3.1 computes the diagonal action including the exponent-zero cases.

The single-node instance is the base of both formulas: step 1.1's bijection and the finite-prefix computations of steps 2.1 and 2.2 are read at the smallest nonzero configuration, where exactly one entry shifts.

The degenerate collision case where a node is unavailable is handled: steps 2.1 and 2.2 zero the term when the shifted entry collides with a neighbour, and the wrap of residues is included since colors are read modulo the rank.

The finite support of a label is the endpoint datum: step 1.1 shows the partition is eventually constant so the word is eventually the ground tail, and the sums range over the finitely many corners of the diagram, whose extreme rows and columns are both covered.

The bijection is an explicit formula and the operators are the stable finite-prefix coproduct actions, so no family is selected from and no choice principle is used. The Statement's explicit bijection is the only map involved.

boundaries.reason: The item constructs a bijection and formulas; it asserts no biconditional, so the forward axis of an equivalence carries no obligation.
No reverse implication is claimed: the formulas are read off the finite-prefix action directly, and no converse statement or uniqueness claim is present.

citations.quote:
For every $N\ge1$ the normally ordered wedges
$\{u_{m_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{m_N}:m_1>m_2>\cdots>m_N\}$ of
[[def-finite-q-wedge-space-and-normal-ordering-relations]] form a
$\mathbb Q(q)$-basis of $W_N$ and an $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-basis of the
Laurent lattice $W_A$. The straightening algorithm terminates with a
well-founded profile: the total index sum and the ambient index interval are
preserved, secondary pairs become strictly more balanced in the sorted
dominance profile, and a leading adjacent swap decreases the inversion count;
in particular no bound by the initial inversion count alone is used. The
local $A_0$-chart $L_0:=A_0W_0$, where $A_0=\mathbb Q[q]_{(q)}$ and $W_0$
is the separate $\mathbb Z[q]$-span of the normal wedges, is a crystal basis: for each color $i$, on the occupied set of a normal tuple
the disjoint pairs $(u_{i+ke},u_{i+ke+1})$ behave as two-vertex highest-weight
$1$ strings, empty and doubly occupied pairs are frozen, and a shift of an
index by one either stays ordered or collides to zero; hence the residues of
the ordered wedges are stable under the normalized string operators and give a
crystal of the integrable affine wedge module. The image of the full
$\mathbb Z[q]$-tensor lattice need not equal $W_0$, and negative powers of $q$
in the straightening are not asserted to be triangular at $q=0$.

Let $F^{(M)}$ be the charge-$M$ Fock space with ground sequence
$b^\circ_s=u_{M-s}$ and let $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ be the opposite-channel energy.
Then:

(i) **Vanishing against the right tail.** For a fixed type-A ground sequence,
the condition $H_{\mathrm{op}}(b\otimes b^\circ_s)\le0$ means that the added
integer index lies inside or below the filled right tail
$\{M-s,M-s-1,\dots\}$; then $b\wedge b^\circ_s\wedge b^\circ_{s+1}\wedge\cdots=0$,
a sufficiently long finite prefix of this entire filled-tail wedge is already $0$, and hence the element lies in $q^nW_0$ for
every $n$.

(ii) **Dual left tail.** The mirrored condition with the left tail gives the
same exact finite vanishing, with the roles of left and right exchanged.

(iii) **Endomorphisms commuting with the loop.** A nonzero-weight endomorphism
$C$ of $V_{\mathrm{aff}}$ commuting with $z$ has only finitely many
loop-shift/color terms on each fundamental vector; inserting $C$ deep inside a
ground tail is eventually $0$, so it converges $q$-adically to $0$ on every
vector.

(iv) **The period operator.** For the explicit period operator
$T$ on $F^{(M)}$ that prepends $e$ vacuum entries and shifts every old index
down by $e$: $T$ preserves each label-weight/size component, and on the
positive-size-$n$ part its $k$-th power is $0$ as soon as $ke>n$.
Consequently $(1-T)^{-1}=1+T+T^2+\cdots$ is a finite geometric sum on every
nonvacuum weight, and each label weight has only finitely many partition
vectors.

Fix a **charge** $M\in\mathbb Z$ and let $W_N$ be the finite q-wedge spaces of
[[def-finite-q-wedge-space-and-normal-ordering-relations]]. For $r\le s$ define
the connecting map
$\varphi_{r,s}(u_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{i_r})
=u_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{i_r}\wedge u_{M-r}\wedge u_{M-r-1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{M-s+1}$,
so that new entries are the consecutive ground tail
$u_{M-N},u_{M-N-1},\dots$ appended to a prefix of length $N$. The **charge-$M$
Fock space** is the algebraic direct limit $F^{(M)}:=\varinjlim_{N}W_N$ of the
finite wedge spaces along these maps; equivalently it is the quotient of the
eventually-vacuum tensor space by the local wedge kernels. Write
$|\lambda;M\rangle$ for the image of the normally ordered semi-infinite word
with entries $i_k=M+\lambda_k-k+1$ indexed by the positive parts of the
partition $\lambda$, so that the vacuum $\varnothing$ corresponds to
$u_M\wedge u_{M-1}\wedge u_{M-2}\wedge\cdots$.

The **Laurent, positive and integral charts** of $F^{(M)}$ are

$$F_A:=\bigoplus_{\lambda}A\,|\lambda;M\rangle,\qquad F_0:=\bigoplus_{\lambda}A_0\,|\lambda;M\rangle,\qquad F_{\mathbb Z0}:=\bigoplus_{\lambda}\mathbb Z[q]\,|\lambda;M\rangle,\qquad A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}],\ A_0=\mathbb Q[q]_{(q)}.$$

The **separated q-adic topology** on the full field space is the one induced by
the filtration $q^nF_0$, never by $q^nF_A=F_A$; a finite $A_0$-label component
completes to a $\mathbb Q[\![q]\!]$-lattice, and the full-field component completes
to $\mathbb Q((q))\otimes_{\mathbb Q(q)}F^{(M)}_\mu$ for the label-weight
pieces. Separately, the integral $\mathbb Z[q]$-chart completes to a
$\mathbb Z[\![q]\!]$-lattice; this completion is not identified with
$\mathbb Q((q))$ and is not asserted to carry a $\mathbb Q$-vector-space
topology.

**Vacuum weights.** For $M=j-ae$ with $j\in\{1,\dots,e\}$ and $a\in\mathbb Z$
the vacuum $P$-weight $\Omega_M$ is normalised by $\Omega_0=\Lambda_0$ and
$\Omega_M-\Omega_{M-1}=\mathrm{wt}(u_M)$; explicitly, if $M=te+r$ with
$0\le r<e$, then

$$\Omega_M=\Lambda_r-\Bigl(\frac{e\,t(t-1)}{2}+tr\Bigr)\delta.$$

The weight of the partition $\lambda$ is
$\Omega_M-\sum_{\text{cells}}\alpha_{c-r+M}$, its size $|\lambda|$ is a separate
grading, and the $d$-eigenvalue is $\Omega_M(d)$ minus the number of residue-$0$
cells; no periodicity $\Omega_M=\Omega_{M-e}+\delta$ is asserted.

Let $\lambda\vdash n$ with Young diagram $[\lambda]$, and let
$\mu\vdash n-1$ and $\nu\vdash n+1$ denote partitions of the neighbouring
sizes ([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]).

A node $x\in[\lambda]$ is **removable** if deleting it leaves a Young diagram,
that is, if there is a partition $\mu\vdash n-1$ with
$$[\mu]=[\lambda]\setminus\{x\};$$
such a $\mu$ is unique because a partition is determined by its diagram. A
point $y\notin[\lambda]$ is **addable** for $\lambda$ if inserting it leaves a
Young diagram, that is, if there is a partition $\nu\vdash n+1$ with
$$[\nu]=[\lambda]\cup\{y\};$$
again $\nu$ is unique. We write $\operatorname{Rem}(\lambda)$ and
$\operatorname{Add}(\lambda)$ for the sets of removable and of addable nodes
of $\lambda$.

Since $[\lambda]=\{(i,j):1\le i\le k,\ 1\le j\le\lambda_i\}$ is determined by
the inequalities $1\le j\le\lambda_i$, the two conditions have the following
row form. Write $\lambda_{k+1}:=0$ for a partition $\lambda=(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_k)$.
A node $(i,\lambda_i)$ is removable if and only if
$\lambda_i>\lambda_{i+1}$: deleting the last node of row $i$ keeps the row
lengths weakly decreasing exactly when row $i+1$ is strictly shorter, and no
node $(i,j)$ with $j<\lambda_i$ can be deleted, since the node
$(i,j+1)$ would then have no node to its left. Similarly a node
$(i,\lambda_i+1)$ with $1\le i\le k$ is addable if and only if $i=1$ or
$\lambda_{i-1}>\lambda_i$, the node $(k+1,1)$ opening a new row is always
addable, and these are all the addable nodes. In particular a row endpoint of
$[\lambda]$ is removable only if no node of $[\lambda]$ lies immediately
below it.

For the empty partition the diagram is empty, so
$\operatorname{Rem}(\varnothing)=\emptyset$, while
$\operatorname{Add}(\varnothing)=\{(1,1)\}$ is a single node, whose insertion
produces the partition $(1)$.

**Partitions.** Let $n\ge 0$ be an integer. A **partition of $n$** is a finite
weakly decreasing sequence $\lambda=(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_k)$ of positive
integers with $\lambda_1+\cdots+\lambda_k=n$. Its entries are the **parts** of
$\lambda$ and $k$ is the **number of parts**. For $n=0$ the only partition is
the **empty partition** $\varnothing$, the empty sequence with $k=0$; for
$n\ge 1$ one has $\lambda_1\ge\lambda_2\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_k\ge 1$ and
$k\le n$. We write $\lambda\vdash n$. Trailing zeros are not parts: a finite
sequence of nonnegative integers ending in $0$ is not a partition, so the
number of parts of $\lambda$ is determined by $\lambda$ and
$(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_k)$ is a different data type from
$(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_k,0)$.

**English Young diagrams.** The **(English) Young diagram** of a nonempty $\lambda$ is
$$[\lambda]:=\{\,(i,j)\;:\;1\le i\le k,\ 1\le j\le \lambda_i\,\}\subseteq\mathbb N\times\mathbb N,$$
where $i$ numbers the **rows** downward and $j$ numbers the **columns**
rightward. An element of $[\lambda]$ is a **node**, or box, of the diagram. Row
$i$ of $[\lambda]$ carries $\lambda_i$ nodes, and column $j$ carries
$$\lambda'_j:=\#\{\,i: \lambda_i\ge j\,\}$$
nodes, a quantity that is $0$ beyond the last column (and for every $j\ge1$ when $\lambda=\varnothing$). Since a partition is weakly
decreasing, $[\lambda]$ determines $\lambda$: if $[\mu]=[\lambda]$, then row
$i$ of $[\lambda]$ is row $i$ of $[\mu]$, so $\mu_i=\lambda_i$ for every $i$
and $\mu=\lambda$. In particular $[\varnothing]=\emptyset$, the empty diagram.

**Conjugation.** The **conjugate partition** of a nonempty $\lambda$ is
$$\lambda':=(\lambda'_1,\lambda'_2,\dots,\lambda'_{\lambda_1}),$$
the sequence of column heights of $[\lambda]$, with $\varnothing':=\varnothing$
for the empty partition. This is again a partition of $n$, and
$[\lambda']$ is the transpose of $[\lambda]$:
for $1\le i\le\lambda_1$ and $1\le j\le k$,
$$(i,j)\in[\lambda']\iff j\le\lambda'_i\iff \lambda_j\ge i\iff (j,i)\in[\lambda].$$
Outside these bounds neither diagram contains the corresponding node; for the empty partition both diagrams are empty.
Conjugation is an involution, $\lambda''=\lambda$, because
$\lambda''_i=\#\{j:\lambda'_j\ge i\}$ counts the columns of $[\lambda]$ of
height at least $i$, that is, the columns $j$ with at least $i$ rows of length
$\ge j$, which by weak decrease is exactly the set of $j\le\lambda_i$. Thus
$\lambda\mapsto\lambda'$ is a bijection on the partitions of $n$, exchanging
the number of parts with the largest part for nonempty partitions.

**Size zero.** The symmetric group of $\{1,\dots,n\}$ is
$S_n:=\operatorname{Sym}(\{1,\dots,n\})$ ([[def-symmetric-group]]) for every
$n\ge 0$, and we fix
$$S_0:=\operatorname{Sym}(\emptyset)=\{1\},$$
the trivial group; for $n=0$ the set $\{1,\dots,n\}$ is empty and the group
acts trivially on every size-zero object below. This is the convention used
whenever the constructions of this page are read at $n=0$.

Fix a **charge** $M\in\mathbb Z$ and let $W_N$ be the finite q-wedge spaces of
[[def-finite-q-wedge-space-and-normal-ordering-relations]]. For $r\le s$ define
the connecting map
$\varphi_{r,s}(u_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{i_r})
=u_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{i_r}\wedge u_{M-r}\wedge u_{M-r-1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{M-s+1}$,
so that new entries are the consecutive ground tail
$u_{M-N},u_{M-N-1},\dots$ appended to a prefix of length $N$. The **charge-$M$
Fock space** is the algebraic direct limit $F^{(M)}:=\varinjlim_{N}W_N$ of the
finite wedge spaces along these maps; equivalently it is the quotient of the
eventually-vacuum tensor space by the local wedge kernels. Write
$|\lambda;M\rangle$ for the image of the normally ordered semi-infinite word
with entries $i_k=M+\lambda_k-k+1$ indexed by the positive parts of the
partition $\lambda$, so that the vacuum $\varnothing$ corresponds to
$u_M\wedge u_{M-1}\wedge u_{M-2}\wedge\cdots$.

The **Laurent, positive and integral charts** of $F^{(M)}$ are

$$F_A:=\bigoplus_{\lambda}A\,|\lambda;M\rangle,\qquad F_0:=\bigoplus_{\lambda}A_0\,|\lambda;M\rangle,\qquad F_{\mathbb Z0}:=\bigoplus_{\lambda}\mathbb Z[q]\,|\lambda;M\rangle,\qquad A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}],\ A_0=\mathbb Q[q]_{(q)}.$$

The **separated q-adic topology** on the full field space is the one induced by
the filtration $q^nF_0$, never by $q^nF_A=F_A$; a finite $A_0$-label component
completes to a $\mathbb Q[\![q]\!]$-lattice, and the full-field component completes
to $\mathbb Q((q))\otimes_{\mathbb Q(q)}F^{(M)}_\mu$ for the label-weight
pieces. Separately, the integral $\mathbb Z[q]$-chart completes to a
$\mathbb Z[\![q]\!]$-lattice; this completion is not identified with
$\mathbb Q((q))$ and is not asserted to carry a $\mathbb Q$-vector-space
topology.

**Vacuum weights.** For $M=j-ae$ with $j\in\{1,\dots,e\}$ and $a\in\mathbb Z$
the vacuum $P$-weight $\Omega_M$ is normalised by $\Omega_0=\Lambda_0$ and
$\Omega_M-\Omega_{M-1}=\mathrm{wt}(u_M)$; explicitly, if $M=te+r$ with
$0\le r<e$, then

$$\Omega_M=\Lambda_r-\Bigl(\frac{e\,t(t-1)}{2}+tr\Bigr)\delta.$$

The weight of the partition $\lambda$ is
$\Omega_M-\sum_{\text{cells}}\alpha_{c-r+M}$, its size $|\lambda|$ is a separate
grading, and the $d$-eigenvalue is $\Omega_M(d)$ minus the number of residue-$0$
cells; no periodicity $\Omega_M=\Omega_{M-e}+\delta$ is asserted.

derivations.claim: The bijection and finiteness of the node sums. The map $\lambda\mapsto(i_k)_{k\ge1}$ with $i_k=M+\lambda_k-k+1$ is a bijection onto normal semi-infinite words because $\lambda$ is weakly decreasing and eventually zero, and $i_k$ is strictly decreasing and eventually equal to the ground tail; a partition of size $n$ has at most $n+1$ addable nodes and at most $n$ removable nodes, so both sums in the statement are finite.

The $F_i$ formula. On a prefix of length $N$ containing the support of $|\lambda\rangle$, the coproduct action of $F_i$ shifts a selected entry $i_k$ to $i_k+1$, provided $i_k\equiv i$; if $i_k+1=i_{k-1}$ the resulting term has a collision and vanishes by the wedge relations, and otherwise the shift is exactly the addition of the corner cell $(k,\lambda_k+1)$ of residue $i$ by [F3]. The coefficient is the product of the prefix $K$-eigenvalues of the finite coproduct, which is $q^{A_i^r-R_i^r}$: a frozen doubly occupied $i$-pair contributes net weight $0$, and the singly occupied $i$-pairs are exactly the other addable and removable $i$-corners, ordered by content, contributing $+1$ for each addable corner strictly to the right (higher content) of the added node and $-1$ for each removable one.

The $E_i$ formula. For $E_i$ the finite-prefix coproduct shifts an entry with $i_k\equiv i+1$ to $i_k-1$; if it collides the term is zero, and otherwise it deletes the corner cell $(k,\lambda_k)$ of residue $i$, whose smaller diagram is $\mu-\gamma$. The suffix $K^{-1}$-weight contributes the addable and removable $i$-corners of $\mu-\gamma$ strictly to the left (lower content) of the removed node; the single artificial boundary pair at the cutoff contributes $q^{\delta_{i\equiv M-N}}$ to the finite $E_i$ coefficient, which is cancelled by the factor $q^{-\delta_{i\equiv M-N}}$ in the renormalised operator $q^{-\delta_{i\equiv M-N}}E_i$. The artificial removal at the cutoff duplicates the first appended ground entry and vanishes; after one more ground entry is appended, the same cancellation removes the changed boundary factor. Thus the renormalised operator is cutoff-independent and defines the stable limit by [F2]. The sign is negative because $E_i$ shifts down in the wedge.

The toral operators. The paired occupation count gives $K_i|\lambda\rangle=q^{N_i(\lambda)}|\lambda\rangle$: a doubly occupied color pair contributes total weight zero, while each single occupied pair contributes $+1$ or $-1$, corresponding to an addable or removable corner. The full label in the charge-$M$ space is $\Omega_M-\sum_{\mathrm{cells}}\alpha_{c-r+M}$ from [F3]. Since $\langle\alpha_i,d\rangle=\delta_{i0}$ in the explicit full affine datum, evaluation on $d$ is $\Omega_M(d)-m_0$, so $K_d$ acts by $q^{\Omega_M(d)-m_0}$. In charge zero $\Omega_0(d)=0$, giving $q^{-m_0}$. For general charge replace residues by content plus $M$. This is the degree-torus action on the explicit label; it is not a simultaneous translation of all wedge indices by the loop operator.

Conclusion. Normal wedges are bijective with partitions, and the stable finite-prefix action gives the displayed finite node formulas for $F_i,E_i,K_i,K_d$ before any relation or crystal statement is invoked.

boundaries.evidence: The empty partition is not an afterthought: step 1.1 includes it as the basis image of the vacuum, and its declared weight reduces to Lambda_0 with nodal data supplied by the same formulas, so the highest-weight case is inside the definition.

The charge-zero chamber is fixed and used: residues are the node content modulo the rank at charge zero, and the loop grading acts by the exponent counting residue-zero cells, so the case of no residue-zero cells is distinguished from the size grading by the definitions and used in step 3.1.

The two extreme families at the level of columns are separated by calibration: regular means every part multiplicity is below the rank and restricted means every adjacent difference is below it, and step 2.1 verifies that the partition with one column of full height is restricted but not regular.

A column of height equal to the rank is the degenerate-looking configuration and is allowed: step 2.1 checks exactly this shape against both conditions, confirming that restricted partitions may contain such columns while regular ones may not.

The regular and restricted ends of the dictionary are both covered: step 1.2 rewrites the adjacent-difference condition into the conjugate's column-height condition over the whole index range, and step 3.1 records the resulting dictionary.

The space, its basis, its residue convention and its operators are all declared by explicit formulas, so nothing is selected from a family. The Definition's declared basis and conventions carry the construction.

boundaries.reason: The item fixes a space and a coordinate convention; it asserts no biconditional, so there is no forward branch of an equivalence to discharge.
No converse is claimed: the regular-restricted equivalence is a proved dictionary between two statements, established in step 1.2 by direct rewriting, and no remaining reverse obligation exists.

citations.quote:
Keep the conventions of the charge-$M$ Fock space
[[def-semi-infinite-q-wedge-fock-space-and-q-adic-topology]]. Normal wedges are
bijective with partitions through $i_k=M+\lambda_k-k+1$; in charge $0$ the
vacuum is the empty partition. The stable finite-prefix action defines linear
endomorphisms $F_i,E_i,K_i,K_d$ of $F^{(0)}$ by

$$F_i|\lambda\rangle=\sum_{\text{addable }\gamma\text{ of residue }i}q^{A_i^r-R_i^r}\,|\lambda+\gamma\rangle,\qquad E_i|\mu\rangle=\sum_{\text{removable }\gamma\text{ of residue }i}q^{-(A_i^l-R_i^l)}\,|\mu-\gamma\rangle,$$

where for $F_i$ the counts are taken in the smaller diagram $\lambda$ and count
addable/removable $i$-nodes strictly to the right of the added node (higher
content), and for $E_i$ the counts are taken in the smaller diagram $\mu-\gamma$
and count nodes strictly to the left of the removed node (lower content), with
the removed node excluded; all sums are finite. The toral operators act by
$K_i|\lambda\rangle=q^{N_i(\lambda)}|\lambda\rangle$ with $N_i$ the
addable-minus-removable count, and $K_d|\lambda\rangle=q^{-m_0(\lambda)}|\lambda\rangle$;
the size $|\lambda|$ is a separate grading. Charge $M$ replaces the residues by
content $+M$ and $K_d$ by $\Omega_M(d)-m_0$.

Let $\lambda\vdash n$ with Young diagram $[\lambda]$, and let
$\mu\vdash n-1$ and $\nu\vdash n+1$ denote partitions of the neighbouring
sizes ([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]).

A node $x\in[\lambda]$ is **removable** if deleting it leaves a Young diagram,
that is, if there is a partition $\mu\vdash n-1$ with
$$[\mu]=[\lambda]\setminus\{x\};$$
such a $\mu$ is unique because a partition is determined by its diagram. A
point $y\notin[\lambda]$ is **addable** for $\lambda$ if inserting it leaves a
Young diagram, that is, if there is a partition $\nu\vdash n+1$ with
$$[\nu]=[\lambda]\cup\{y\};$$
again $\nu$ is unique. We write $\operatorname{Rem}(\lambda)$ and
$\operatorname{Add}(\lambda)$ for the sets of removable and of addable nodes
of $\lambda$.

Since $[\lambda]=\{(i,j):1\le i\le k,\ 1\le j\le\lambda_i\}$ is determined by
the inequalities $1\le j\le\lambda_i$, the two conditions have the following
row form. Write $\lambda_{k+1}:=0$ for a partition $\lambda=(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_k)$.
A node $(i,\lambda_i)$ is removable if and only if
$\lambda_i>\lambda_{i+1}$: deleting the last node of row $i$ keeps the row
lengths weakly decreasing exactly when row $i+1$ is strictly shorter, and no
node $(i,j)$ with $j<\lambda_i$ can be deleted, since the node
$(i,j+1)$ would then have no node to its left. Similarly a node
$(i,\lambda_i+1)$ with $1\le i\le k$ is addable if and only if $i=1$ or
$\lambda_{i-1}>\lambda_i$, the node $(k+1,1)$ opening a new row is always
addable, and these are all the addable nodes. In particular a row endpoint of
$[\lambda]$ is removable only if no node of $[\lambda]$ lies immediately
below it.

For the empty partition the diagram is empty, so
$\operatorname{Rem}(\varnothing)=\emptyset$, while
$\operatorname{Add}(\varnothing)=\{(1,1)\}$ is a single node, whose insertion
produces the partition $(1)$.

**Partitions.** Let $n\ge 0$ be an integer. A **partition of $n$** is a finite
weakly decreasing sequence $\lambda=(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_k)$ of positive
integers with $\lambda_1+\cdots+\lambda_k=n$. Its entries are the **parts** of
$\lambda$ and $k$ is the **number of parts**. For $n=0$ the only partition is
the **empty partition** $\varnothing$, the empty sequence with $k=0$; for
$n\ge 1$ one has $\lambda_1\ge\lambda_2\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_k\ge 1$ and
$k\le n$. We write $\lambda\vdash n$. Trailing zeros are not parts: a finite
sequence of nonnegative integers ending in $0$ is not a partition, so the
number of parts of $\lambda$ is determined by $\lambda$ and
$(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_k)$ is a different data type from
$(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_k,0)$.

**English Young diagrams.** The **(English) Young diagram** of a nonempty $\lambda$ is
$$[\lambda]:=\{\,(i,j)\;:\;1\le i\le k,\ 1\le j\le \lambda_i\,\}\subseteq\mathbb N\times\mathbb N,$$
where $i$ numbers the **rows** downward and $j$ numbers the **columns**
rightward. An element of $[\lambda]$ is a **node**, or box, of the diagram. Row
$i$ of $[\lambda]$ carries $\lambda_i$ nodes, and column $j$ carries
$$\lambda'_j:=\#\{\,i: \lambda_i\ge j\,\}$$
nodes, a quantity that is $0$ beyond the last column (and for every $j\ge1$ when $\lambda=\varnothing$). Since a partition is weakly
decreasing, $[\lambda]$ determines $\lambda$: if $[\mu]=[\lambda]$, then row
$i$ of $[\lambda]$ is row $i$ of $[\mu]$, so $\mu_i=\lambda_i$ for every $i$
and $\mu=\lambda$. In particular $[\varnothing]=\emptyset$, the empty diagram.

**Conjugation.** The **conjugate partition** of a nonempty $\lambda$ is
$$\lambda':=(\lambda'_1,\lambda'_2,\dots,\lambda'_{\lambda_1}),$$
the sequence of column heights of $[\lambda]$, with $\varnothing':=\varnothing$
for the empty partition. This is again a partition of $n$, and
$[\lambda']$ is the transpose of $[\lambda]$:
for $1\le i\le\lambda_1$ and $1\le j\le k$,
$$(i,j)\in[\lambda']\iff j\le\lambda'_i\iff \lambda_j\ge i\iff (j,i)\in[\lambda].$$
Outside these bounds neither diagram contains the corresponding node; for the empty partition both diagrams are empty.
Conjugation is an involution, $\lambda''=\lambda$, because
$\lambda''_i=\#\{j:\lambda'_j\ge i\}$ counts the columns of $[\lambda]$ of
height at least $i$, that is, the columns $j$ with at least $i$ rows of length
$\ge j$, which by weak decrease is exactly the set of $j\le\lambda_i$. Thus
$\lambda\mapsto\lambda'$ is a bijection on the partitions of $n$, exchanging
the number of parts with the largest part for nonempty partitions.

**Size zero.** The symmetric group of $\{1,\dots,n\}$ is
$S_n:=\operatorname{Sym}(\{1,\dots,n\})$ ([[def-symmetric-group]]) for every
$n\ge 0$, and we fix
$$S_0:=\operatorname{Sym}(\emptyset)=\{1\},$$
the trivial group; for $n=0$ the set $\{1,\dots,n\}$ is empty and the group
acts trivially on every size-zero object below. This is the convention used
whenever the constructions of this page are read at $n=0$.

derivations.claim: The partition basis and the declared operators. By [F1] the map $\lambda\mapsto|\lambda\rangle$ is a bijection from partitions to normal semi-infinite words and the stable prefix action gives well-defined linear $F_i,E_i,K_i,K_d$; the weights, residues and size grading are read off literally from $i_k=\lambda_k-k+1$, so the Definition introduces no new structure beyond the wedge construction.

The regular/restricted equivalence. For a partition $\lambda$ and $r\ge1$, the number of columns of height exactly $r$ in $\lambda$ is $\lambda'_r-\lambda'_{r+1}$ where $\lambda'$ is the conjugate; evaluating at $r=\lambda_i$ shows that $\lambda_r-\lambda_{r+1}$ is the multiplicity of the column of height $r$ in $\lambda'$, with $\lambda_r-\lambda_{r+1}=0$ exactly when no column of height $r$ exists. Hence $\lambda$ is $e$-restricted (all adjacent differences $<e$) if and only if its conjugate has all part multiplicities $<e$, that is, if and only if $\lambda'$ is $e$-regular; a column of height $e$ is allowed in an $e$-restricted partition because it contributes adjacent difference $e-1<e$.

The boundary example. For $e\ge2$ the partition $(1^e)$ has parts of multiplicity exactly $e$, so it is not $e$-regular, while its adjacent differences are $1,1,\dots,1,1<e$, so it is $e$-restricted; this shows the two conditions are genuinely different and that the full Fock space contains non-regular labels. All partitions are vertices of the full Fock module; the regular ones will be the labels of the empty component.

Conclusion. The level-one partition Fock space is the charge-$0$ Fock space with weight $\Lambda_0-\sum_im_i\alpha_i$ and residues $c-r\bmod e$, its operators are the stable finite-prefix node operators, and the $e$-regular and $e$-restricted conventions are conjugate to each other with the column-height dictionary.

boundaries.evidence: The empty partition is the induction base: step 1.1 computes the count equal to delta on the zero residue and verifies the claimed formula there, so the base of the induction is not the trivial omission it might look like.

Vanishing counts are treated: step 2.1 computes how each count changes by one under adding a node, including entries that remain zero, and step 3.1's sum over colors equal to one forces compensating zeros and nonzeros across residues.

The singleton partition is the first induction step: step 2.1 starts from the empty partition and adds its unique node, reaching the partition with one cell and matching the general local step at its smallest instance.

The cyclic degenerate case is included: step 2.1's change formula is valid for every residue of the added node, in particular the double-edge entries at rank two where the two colors interact with coefficient minus two.
The boundary color carrying the affine correction is treated in the base step, and step 3.1 sums over all colors to obtain the total one, pinning the endpoint constant of the pairing.
The counts are finite combinatorial data of a given partition and step 2.1's induction runs over its cells, so no family is selected from and the identity is choice-free.

boundaries.reason: The statement is an identity between counts and a pairing together with its listed consequences; no biconditional is asserted, so the forward axis is empty.
There is no converse direction: the identity is proved by induction in steps 1.1 through 3.1, and no equivalence with a second condition is claimed.

citations.quote:
Let $\lambda\vdash n$ with Young diagram $[\lambda]$, and let
$\mu\vdash n-1$ and $\nu\vdash n+1$ denote partitions of the neighbouring
sizes ([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]).

A node $x\in[\lambda]$ is **removable** if deleting it leaves a Young diagram,
that is, if there is a partition $\mu\vdash n-1$ with
$$[\mu]=[\lambda]\setminus\{x\};$$
such a $\mu$ is unique because a partition is determined by its diagram. A
point $y\notin[\lambda]$ is **addable** for $\lambda$ if inserting it leaves a
Young diagram, that is, if there is a partition $\nu\vdash n+1$ with
$$[\nu]=[\lambda]\cup\{y\};$$
again $\nu$ is unique. We write $\operatorname{Rem}(\lambda)$ and
$\operatorname{Add}(\lambda)$ for the sets of removable and of addable nodes
of $\lambda$.

Since $[\lambda]=\{(i,j):1\le i\le k,\ 1\le j\le\lambda_i\}$ is determined by
the inequalities $1\le j\le\lambda_i$, the two conditions have the following
row form. Write $\lambda_{k+1}:=0$ for a partition $\lambda=(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_k)$.
A node $(i,\lambda_i)$ is removable if and only if
$\lambda_i>\lambda_{i+1}$: deleting the last node of row $i$ keeps the row
lengths weakly decreasing exactly when row $i+1$ is strictly shorter, and no
node $(i,j)$ with $j<\lambda_i$ can be deleted, since the node
$(i,j+1)$ would then have no node to its left. Similarly a node
$(i,\lambda_i+1)$ with $1\le i\le k$ is addable if and only if $i=1$ or
$\lambda_{i-1}>\lambda_i$, the node $(k+1,1)$ opening a new row is always
addable, and these are all the addable nodes. In particular a row endpoint of
$[\lambda]$ is removable only if no node of $[\lambda]$ lies immediately
below it.

For the empty partition the diagram is empty, so
$\operatorname{Rem}(\varnothing)=\emptyset$, while
$\operatorname{Add}(\varnothing)=\{(1,1)\}$ is a single node, whose insertion
produces the partition $(1)$.

Let $F:=\bigoplus_{\lambda}\mathbb Q(q)|\lambda\rangle$ be the charge-$0$ part of
the Fock space of
[[lem-semi-infinite-wedges-are-indexed-by-partitions-and-give-node-action-formulas]],
with basis indexed by all partitions and with the node operators $F_i,E_i$
defined by the stable finite-prefix action. Assign to $|\lambda\rangle$ the
**level-one weight**

$$\mathrm{wt}(|\lambda\rangle):=\Lambda_0-\sum_{i\in I}m_i(\lambda)\,\alpha_i, \qquad m_i(\lambda):=\#\{\text{cells of }\lambda\text{ of residue }i\},$$

where the **residue** of a cell in row $r$ and column $c$ is $c-r\bmod e$, and
the **size** $|\lambda|$ is the separate grading. The vacuum is the empty
partition $\varnothing$; $F_i$ adds and $E_i$ removes a node by the explicit
finite node formulas of the same item. The toral action is
$K_i|\lambda\rangle=q^{N_i(\lambda)}|\lambda\rangle$ with $N_i$ the
addable-minus-removable count, proved to be the Cartan pairing in
[[lem-the-node-count-is-the-level-one-cartan-pairing]], and
$K_d|\lambda\rangle=q^{-m_0(\lambda)}|\lambda\rangle$.

A partition is **$e$-regular** if each positive part occurs with multiplicity
$<e$, and **$e$-restricted** if $\lambda_r-\lambda_{r+1}<e$ for every $r\ge1$
(with $\lambda_{r}=0$ beyond the length). These operators are declared linear
endomorphisms here; the affine relations proved later establish the actual
module structure, so nothing about $F$ is silently assumed in this Definition.

Fix an integer $e\ge 2$ and put $I:=\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z=\{0,1,\dots,e-1\}$
with its cyclic order; elements of $I$ are called **residues**. Let
$A=(a_{ij})_{i,j\in I}$ be the integer matrix with

$$a_{ii}=2,\qquad a_{i,i-1}=a_{i,i+1}=-1\ \ (i\in I)$$

when $e\ge 3$, and with $a_{00}=a_{11}=2$ and the single double edge
$a_{01}=a_{10}=-2$ when $e=2$; all indices are read modulo $e$. Thus for
$e\ge3$ all off-diagonal entries other than the neighbouring entries $-1$ are
$0$, and for $e=2$ the matrix is
$\begin{pmatrix}2&-2\\-2&2\end{pmatrix}$. Take the diagonal symmetrizer
$D=\operatorname{diag}(1,\dots,1)$ and the quantum parameter $q$ over
$\mathbb Q$, so that $q_i=q^{d_i}=q$ for every $i\in I$
([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]).

Choose free abelian groups

$$P=\Bigl(\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z\Lambda_i\Bigr)\oplus\mathbb Z\delta, \qquad P^{\vee}=\Bigl(\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z h_i\Bigr)\oplus\mathbb Z d,$$

with the $\mathbb Z$-bilinear pairing $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle:P\times
P^{\vee}\to\mathbb Z$ determined by

$$\langle\Lambda_j,h_i\rangle=\delta_{ij},\qquad \langle\delta,h_i\rangle=0,\qquad \langle\Lambda_j,d\rangle=0,\qquad \langle\delta,d\rangle=1 .$$

Define the **simple roots**

$$\alpha_i:=\sum_{j\in I}a_{ji}\Lambda_j+\delta_{i0}\,\delta\qquad(i\in I),$$

let $Q:=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z\alpha_i\subseteq P$ be the **root lattice**
and $Q^+$ its nonnegative cone, and define the **central element**
$c:=\sum_{i\in I}h_i\in P^{\vee}$. The **level** of $\lambda\in P$ is
$\langle c,\lambda\rangle\in\mathbb Z$ ([[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]),
and the **classical weight lattice** is $P_{\mathrm{cl}}:=P/\mathbb Z\delta$.

The **diagram reflection** $\tau$ is the pair of $\mathbb Z$-linear
involutions $\tau:P\to P$, $P^{\vee}\to P^{\vee}$ with
$\tau(\Lambda_i)=\Lambda_{-i}$, $\tau(\delta)=\delta$, $\tau(h_i)=h_{-i}$ and
$\tau(d)=d$ (indices negated in $\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$).

The **normalized affine weight form** is the symmetric $\mathbb Q$-bilinear form on $P_{\mathbb Q}:=P\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q$ determined, in the decomposition $P_{\mathbb Q}=Q_{\mathbb Q}\oplus\mathbb Q\Lambda_0$, by

$$(\alpha_i,\alpha_j)=a_{ij},\qquad (\Lambda_0,\alpha_i)=\delta_{i0},\qquad (\Lambda_0,\Lambda_0)=0.$$

Thus, for $x=\sum_i x_i\alpha_i$, $y=\sum_i y_i\alpha_i$ and $t,s\in\mathbb Q$, set

$$(x+t\Lambda_0,y+s\Lambda_0)=\sum_{i,j}x_i a_{ij}y_j+t y_0+s x_0.$$

In particular $(\lambda,\alpha_i)=\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle$ and $(\lambda,\delta)=\langle\lambda,c\rangle$. Its restriction to $Q$ is integer-valued; on all of $P$ it is rational-valued. This form on weights is distinct from the weight-coweight pairing. Define $s_i(\lambda):=\lambda-\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle\alpha_i$ and let $W$ be the group generated by these simple reflections; the form is $W$-invariant and $\tau$-invariant.

derivations.claim: The empty partition. The empty partition has exactly one addable node, the cell $(1,1)$ of residue $0$, and no removable nodes; hence $N_i(\varnothing)=\delta_{i0}$. The right-hand side is $\delta_{i0}-\sum_ja_{ij}\cdot0=\delta_{i0}$.

The local step. Let $\mu$ be obtained from $\lambda$ by adding a node $\gamma$ of residue $k$. In $\mu$ the new node $\gamma$ is removable of residue $k$, and the addable/removable status of the other boundary nodes changes exactly at the neighbours of $\gamma$: the node $(r,\lambda_r+1)$ stops being addable and the node $(r+1,\lambda_{r+1})$ stops being removable precisely when they are absorbed or released by the new corner, and their residues are $\lambda_r+1-r$ and $\lambda_{r+1}-(r+1)=k-1$ and $k+1$ shifted by the local geometry, i.e. consecutive to $k$. Bookkeeping the corners of the skew shape $\mu/\lambda$ gives $N_i(\mu)-N_i(\lambda)=-\bigl(2\delta_{ik}-\delta_{i,k-1}-\delta_{i,k+1}\bigr)=-a_{ik}$, and $m_j(\mu)=m_j(\lambda)+\delta_{jk}$; hence the right-hand side changes by $-\sum_ja_{ij}\delta_{jk}=-a_{ik}$ as well, and the identity is preserved.

The identity and its consequences. Induction on the number of cells from step 1.1 with the local step 2.1 gives $N_i(\lambda)=\delta_{i0}-\sum_ja_{ij}m_j(\lambda)$ for every partition. Summing over $i$ and using $\sum_ia_{ij}=0$ and $\sum_i\delta_{i0}=1$ gives $\sum_iN_i(\lambda)=1$. Therefore the toral action $K_i|\lambda\rangle=q^{N_i(\lambda)}|\lambda\rangle$ equals $q^{\delta_{i0}-\sum_ja_{ij}m_j}=q^{\langle h_i,\Lambda_0-\sum_jm_j\alpha_j\rangle}$, and the product over $i$ acts by $q^{\sum_iN_i}=q$, so $\mathrm{wt}(|\lambda\rangle)=\Lambda_0-\sum_jm_j\alpha_j$ has $\langle c,\mathrm{wt}\rangle=\sum_iN_i=1$ and level one; adding a node of residue $k$ replaces $m_k$ by $m_k+1$, changing the weight by $-\alpha_k$ and $N_i$ by $-a_{ik}$.

Conclusion. The addable-minus-removable count is the level-one Cartan pairing, the sum of the counts is $1$, the central product acts by $q$, and the declared toral action of the partition Fock space is the one required for a level-one module.

boundaries.evidence: The empty partition is vacuous-safe by the definitions: there are no removable nodes, and the unique addable node of residue zero has no nodes strictly above or below it, which step 1.1's three-class splitting records.

A node with no siblings strictly above or below has both signed exponents zero, and step 1.1 proves the splitting identity by partitioning the node set into the node itself, the larger-content ones and the smaller-content ones.

The smallest nonzero configurations are covered by the general statement: step 1.1 splits the node set into three disjoint classes, and step 1.3 instantiates the definitions at rank two on the partition with three cells in the first row and one in the second.

The rank-two double-edge calibration is an explicit numbered step: step 1.3 lists the addable and removable nodes of both residues with their contents, and the definitions make no coprimality or genericity assumption.

Let $F:=\bigoplus_{\lambda}\mathbb Q(q)|\lambda\rangle$ be the charge-$0$ part of
the Fock space of
[[lem-semi-infinite-wedges-are-indexed-by-partitions-and-give-node-action-formulas]],
with basis indexed by all partitions and with the node operators $F_i,E_i$
defined by the stable finite-prefix action. Assign to $|\lambda\rangle$ the
**level-one weight**

$$\mathrm{wt}(|\lambda\rangle):=\Lambda_0-\sum_{i\in I}m_i(\lambda)\,\alpha_i, \qquad m_i(\lambda):=\#\{\text{cells of }\lambda\text{ of residue }i\},$$

where the **residue** of a cell in row $r$ and column $c$ is $c-r\bmod e$, and
the **size** $|\lambda|$ is the separate grading. The vacuum is the empty
partition $\varnothing$; $F_i$ adds and $E_i$ removes a node by the explicit
finite node formulas of the same item. The toral action is
$K_i|\lambda\rangle=q^{N_i(\lambda)}|\lambda\rangle$ with $N_i$ the
addable-minus-removable count, proved to be the Cartan pairing in
[[lem-the-node-count-is-the-level-one-cartan-pairing]], and
$K_d|\lambda\rangle=q^{-m_0(\lambda)}|\lambda\rangle$.

A partition is **$e$-regular** if each positive part occurs with multiplicity
$<e$, and **$e$-restricted** if $\lambda_r-\lambda_{r+1}<e$ for every $r\ge1$
(with $\lambda_{r}=0$ beyond the length). These operators are declared linear
endomorphisms here; the affine relations proved later establish the actual
module structure, so nothing about $F$ is silently assumed in this Definition.

Let $\lambda\vdash n$ with Young diagram $[\lambda]$, and let
$\mu\vdash n-1$ and $\nu\vdash n+1$ denote partitions of the neighbouring
sizes ([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]).

A node $x\in[\lambda]$ is **removable** if deleting it leaves a Young diagram,
that is, if there is a partition $\mu\vdash n-1$ with
$$[\mu]=[\lambda]\setminus\{x\};$$
such a $\mu$ is unique because a partition is determined by its diagram. A
point $y\notin[\lambda]$ is **addable** for $\lambda$ if inserting it leaves a
Young diagram, that is, if there is a partition $\nu\vdash n+1$ with
$$[\nu]=[\lambda]\cup\{y\};$$
again $\nu$ is unique. We write $\operatorname{Rem}(\lambda)$ and
$\operatorname{Add}(\lambda)$ for the sets of removable and of addable nodes
of $\lambda$.

Since $[\lambda]=\{(i,j):1\le i\le k,\ 1\le j\le\lambda_i\}$ is determined by
the inequalities $1\le j\le\lambda_i$, the two conditions have the following
row form. Write $\lambda_{k+1}:=0$ for a partition $\lambda=(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_k)$.
A node $(i,\lambda_i)$ is removable if and only if
$\lambda_i>\lambda_{i+1}$: deleting the last node of row $i$ keeps the row
lengths weakly decreasing exactly when row $i+1$ is strictly shorter, and no
node $(i,j)$ with $j<\lambda_i$ can be deleted, since the node
$(i,j+1)$ would then have no node to its left. Similarly a node
$(i,\lambda_i+1)$ with $1\le i\le k$ is addable if and only if $i=1$ or
$\lambda_{i-1}>\lambda_i$, the node $(k+1,1)$ opening a new row is always
addable, and these are all the addable nodes. In particular a row endpoint of
$[\lambda]$ is removable only if no node of $[\lambda]$ lies immediately
below it.

For the empty partition the diagram is empty, so
$\operatorname{Rem}(\varnothing)=\emptyset$, while
$\operatorname{Add}(\varnothing)=\{(1,1)\}$ is a single node, whose insertion
produces the partition $(1)$.

For every partition $\lambda$, every residue $i\in I$, and
$N_i(\lambda):=\#\{\text{addable }i\text{-nodes of }\lambda\}
-\#\{\text{removable }i\text{-nodes of }\lambda\}$ one has

$$N_i(\lambda)=\delta_{i0}-\sum_{j\in I}a_{ij}\,m_j(\lambda),$$

where $m_j(\lambda)$ is the number of residue-$j$ cells of $\lambda$ and
$A=(a_{ij})$ is the cyclic affine type $A$ Cartan matrix. Consequently
$\sum_{i\in I}N_i(\lambda)=1$; the toral operator acts by
$K_i|\lambda\rangle=q^{N_i(\lambda)}|\lambda\rangle=q^{\langle
h_i,\mathrm{wt}(|\lambda\rangle)\rangle}$, the central product
$K_0K_1\cdots K_{e-1}$ acts by $q$, and $\mathrm{wt}(|\lambda\rangle)
=\Lambda_0-\sum_jm_j\alpha_j$ has level $1$. In particular
$N_i(\varnothing)=\delta_{i0}$, and adding a node of residue $k$ changes $N_i$
by $-a_{ik}$, hence the weight by $-\alpha_k$.

derivations.claim:
The splitting identity. For an addable $i$-node $\gamma$ of $\lambda$, the addable $i$-nodes of $\lambda$ are $\{\gamma\}$, the nodes strictly above $\gamma$ in content and those strictly below, and likewise for the removable $i$-nodes; hence, with the two signed counts of the Definition,
$N_i^r(\lambda,\gamma)+N_i^l(\lambda,\gamma)=\bigl(\#\text{addable}_i(\lambda)-1\bigr)-\#\text{removable}_i(\lambda)=N_i(\lambda)-1$,
because $\gamma$ contributes to the addable count but to neither signed count and no removable node equals $\gamma$. The analogous identity holds for a removable node with $\mu$ and $\lambda$ exchanged.

The node formulas are the ones of the stable prefix action. By the content order, the finite-prefix coefficient of an added node is the product of the suffix $K$-weights, which is exactly $q^{N_i^r}$ (each addable $i$-node to the right contributes $+1$, each removable $i$-node to the right contributes $-1$), and for a removed node the renormalised prefix coefficient is $q^{-N_i^l}$ with the smaller diagram $\mu-\gamma$; these are the formulas (38)-(39) of the stable action, restated in the content order.

Calibration at $e=2$. Take $\lambda=(3,1)$. Its cells have contents $0,1,2$ in row $1$ and $-1$ in row $2$, so mod $2$ the residues are $0,1,0,1$. The addable $0$-nodes are $(2,2)$, content $0$, and $(3,1)$, content $-2$; the removable $0$-node is $(1,3)$, content $2$. For $\gamma=(2,2)$: no addable $0$-node lies above content $0$ and the removable node $(1,3)$ does, so $N_0^r=-1$ and the coefficient of $|3,2\rangle$ is $q^{-1}$; for $\gamma=(3,1)$: the addable $(2,2)$ and the removable $(1,3)$ both lie above content $-2$, so $N_0^r=0$ and the coefficient of $|3,1,1\rangle$ is $1$; hence $F_0|3,1\rangle=q^{-1}|3,2\rangle+|3,1,1\rangle$, which is Leclerc's Exercise 15 value. For $E_0|3,1\rangle$: the only removable $0$-node is $\gamma=(1,3)$, whose smaller diagram is $\lambda=(2,1)$; inside $(2,1)$ the addable $0$-nodes below content $2$ are $(2,2)$ (content $0$) and $(3,1)$ (content $-2$), while no removable $0$-node lies below, so $N_0^l=2$ and $E_0|3,1\rangle=q^{-2}|2,1\rangle$, again matching the calibration.

Conclusion. The node order is the increasing-content order on the boundary nodes, the signed exponents satisfy $N_i^r+N_i^l=N_i(\lambda)-1$ at every node, the node formulas are the ones produced by the stable prefix action, and the $e=2$ calibration reproduces Leclerc's Exercise 15; no tilde operator is obtained by setting $q=0$ in these possibly singular coefficients.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$, an index $i\in I$, and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra and let $A_i$ be the subalgebra generated by $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$ ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]); write $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$ for the divided powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]].

(i) The assignment $e\mapsto E_i$, $f\mapsto F_i$, $k\mapsto K_i$, $k^{-1}\mapsto K_i^{-1}$ defines an algebra isomorphism from the standard rank-one algebra $\mathbb A$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$, presented by $e,f,k^{\pm1}$ with $kek^{-1}=q_i^2e$, $kfk^{-1}=q_i^{-2}f$ and $[e,f]=(k-k^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ onto $A_i$; the images of the monomials $F_i^aK_i^mE_i^b$ ($a,b\ge0$, $m\in\mathbb Z$) are linearly independent in $U_q(\mathfrak g)$, being images of the PBW monomials of the triangular decomposition ([[thm-triangular-decomposition-of-a-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]).

(ii) For all $a,b\ge0$, $K_iE_i^{(a)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{2a}E_i^{(a)}$ and $K_iF_i^{(b)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{-2b}F_i^{(b)}$, and for $b\ge1$ the divided powers satisfy the exact commutation formula
$$E_iF_i^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}E_i+\frac{F_i^{(b-1)}}{q_i^{b}-q_i^{-b}}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}\bigl(q_i^{-2s}K_i-q_i^{2s}K_i^{-1}\bigr);$$
iterating it computes $E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}$ as a finite sum of monomials $F_i^{(b-t)}K_i^{m}E_i^{(a-t)}$ ($0\le t\le\min(a,b)$) with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$.

(iii) For every $N\ge0$ there is a simple $A_i$-module $L_i(N)$ of dimension $N+1$: it is the quotient of the cyclic module $\widetilde M(N):=A_i/\bigl(A_iE_i+A_i(K_i-q_i^N)\bigr)$ by the submodule generated by $F_i^{(N+1)}w_N$, where $w_N$ is the image of $1$, with basis the images $v_t$ of $F_i^{(t)}w_N$, $0\le t\le N$, on which $K_iv_t=q_i^{N-2t}v_t$, $F_iv_t=[t+1]_iv_{t+1}$ and $E_iv_t=[N-t+1]_iv_{t-1}$ (with $v_{-1}=v_{N+1}=0$); $L_i(N)$ is the unique simple $A_i$-module generated by a vector $v\ne0$ with $E_iv=0$, $K_iv=q_i^Nv$ and $F_i^{N+1}v=0$.

Let $M_1,M_2$ be integrable chosen $P$-graded type-one quantum weight modules with crystal bases $(L_1,B_1)$, $(L_2,B_2)$ ([[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]), and let $M_1\otimes M_2$ be the integrable module of [[lem-tensor-products-of-integrable-weight-modules-are-integrable]].

Then $(L_1\otimes_{A_0}L_2,\,B_1\otimes B_2)$ is a crystal basis of $M_1\otimes M_2$, and its crystal is the tensor product crystal $B_1\otimes B_2$ of [[def-tensor-product-of-crystals]]: for all $b_1\in B_1$, $b_2\in B_2$ and $i\in I$,

$$\tilde f_i(b_1\otimes b_2)=\begin{cases}\tilde f_ib_1\otimes b_2,&\varphi_i(b_1)>\varepsilon_i(b_2),\\ b_1\otimes\tilde f_ib_2,&\varphi_i(b_1)\le\varepsilon_i(b_2),\end{cases}\qquad \tilde e_i(b_1\otimes b_2)=\begin{cases}\tilde e_ib_1\otimes b_2,&\varphi_i(b_1)\ge\varepsilon_i(b_2),\\ b_1\otimes\tilde e_ib_2,&\varphi_i(b_1)<\varepsilon_i(b_2),\end{cases}$$

with value $0$ as soon as the selected factor maps to $0$. In particular $\tilde e_i$ and $\tilde f_i$ map $B_1\otimes B_2$ into $(B_1\otimes B_2)\cup\{0\}$, and for all $b,b'\in B_1\otimes B_2$ one has $\tilde f_ib=b'$ if and only if $b=\tilde e_ib'$, so the partial-inverse axiom holds. The equality case $\varphi_i(b_1)=\varepsilon_i(b_2)$ is resolved as in the definition: $\tilde f_i$ acts on the second factor and $\tilde e_i$ on the first.

No finite dimensionality, bounded support or uniform nilpotence is assumed, and no choice principle is used.

derivations.claim: Independence of the $i$-slots. If two $i$-cells are toggled, the neighbours determining each corner's availability are of residues $i\pm1$, and the toggled cell has residue $i$, so it is not a neighbour of any other $i$-cell; hence toggling one $i$-cell never changes the availability of another, every subset of the finitely many slots is realizable, and the orbit is a Boolean cube with $2^k$ distinct partition diagrams.

The cube is the rank-one tensor power. In decreasing-content order, the $j$-th slot's toggling multiplies by $q^{+1}$ or $q^{-1}$ according to occupancy and the iterated coproduct coefficient at slot $j$ is $q^{\sum_{\text{slots before }j}\text{weight}}$ for $f$ and $q^{-\sum_{\text{slots after }j}\text{weight}}$ for $e$; these are exactly $N_i^r$ and $-N_i^l$ by [F3], so the map from tensor bit vectors to partitions is a rank-one module isomorphism onto the cube.

The string rule and lattice stability. Applying the rank-one tensor rule [F2] to the cube and unrolling the strict/non-strict comparison gives: cancel $+-\,$ in decreasing order, then $f$ acts on the first surviving $+$ and $e$ on the last surviving $-$, with zero endpoints when no such sign survives; in increasing order the mirrored statement cancels $-+$ and takes the last $+$ / first $-$. Since all divided powers of order $\ge2$ vanish on each two-vertex factor, every divided $E$- and $F$-power has a Laurent-integral matrix on the cube, so the raw $A_0$-span of partitions is stable under the actual normalized string operators; the standard partition form is the normalized rank-one polarization because it satisfies $(F_i\lambda,\lambda+\gamma)=q^{N_i^r}$ and the adjoint relation transports to the same exponent.

Conclusion. Each fixed-residue orbit is a finite Boolean tensor cube of highest-weight-$1$ strings, the actual normalized string rule is the survivor rule in either content order, including $e=2$, and lattice stability of the raw partition span follows before any congruence is transported.

derivations.claim: The reduction is well defined. The word reduction $-+\to$ empty is the stack matching familiar from bracket sequences: any two adjacent cancellable pairs are either disjoint or share a letter, and the survivors of the stack algorithm do not depend on the order of deletions; equivalently, the unmatched letters are those that are matched by a stack scan, and reversing the word and exchanging $+$ and $-$ exchanges first/last and minus/plus. Hence the good and cogood nodes are well defined by the word alone.

The operator interpretation. By the cube lemma [F1] the actual normalized operators select exactly the survivors: $e_i$ removes the good (first surviving minus) node and $f_i$ adds the cogood (last surviving plus) node, with value $0$ when the respective sign is absent; the equivalent decreasing-content description cancels $+-$ and takes the last surviving $-$ and the first surviving $+$, which is the usual Fayers good-deletion/cogood-addition convention.

Calibrations and the minimiser warning. At $e=3$, $\lambda=(2,1)$ and $i=2$: the addable $2$-nodes are $(1,3)$ and $(2,2)$ in increasing content order, the signature is $++$, so the cogood node is the last plus, the top-right cell $(1,3)$; it is not the leftmost opening $(2,1)$ of a naive minimiser. For every partition $\lambda$, every residue $i\in I$, and
$N_i(\lambda):=\#\{\text{addable }i\text{-nodes of }\lambda\}
-\#\{\text{removable }i\text{-nodes of }\lambda\}$ one has

$$N_i(\lambda)=\delta_{i0}-\sum_{j\in I}a_{ij}\,m_j(\lambda),$$

where $m_j(\lambda)$ is the number of residue-$j$ cells of $\lambda$ and
$A=(a_{ij})$ is the cyclic affine type $A$ Cartan matrix. Consequently
$\sum_{i\in I}N_i(\lambda)=1$; the toral operator acts by
$K_i|\lambda\rangle=q^{N_i(\lambda)}|\lambda\rangle=q^{\langle
h_i,\mathrm{wt}(|\lambda\rangle)\rangle}$, the central product
$K_0K_1\cdots K_{e-1}$ acts by $q$, and $\mathrm{wt}(|\lambda\rangle)
=\Lambda_0-\sum_jm_j\alpha_j$ has level $1$. In particular
$N_i(\varnothing)=\delta_{i0}$, and adding a node of residue $k$ changes $N_i$
by $-a_{ik}$, hence the weight by $-\alpha_k$.

Let $F:=\bigoplus_{\lambda}\mathbb Q(q)|\lambda\rangle$ be the charge-$0$ part of
the Fock space of
[[lem-semi-infinite-wedges-are-indexed-by-partitions-and-give-node-action-formulas]],
with basis indexed by all partitions and with the node operators $F_i,E_i$
defined by the stable finite-prefix action. Assign to $|\lambda\rangle$ the
**level-one weight**

$$\mathrm{wt}(|\lambda\rangle):=\Lambda_0-\sum_{i\in I}m_i(\lambda)\,\alpha_i, \qquad m_i(\lambda):=\#\{\text{cells of }\lambda\text{ of residue }i\},$$

where the **residue** of a cell in row $r$ and column $c$ is $c-r\bmod e$, and
the **size** $|\lambda|$ is the separate grading. The vacuum is the empty
partition $\varnothing$; $F_i$ adds and $E_i$ removes a node by the explicit
finite node formulas of the same item. The toral action is
$K_i|\lambda\rangle=q^{N_i(\lambda)}|\lambda\rangle$ with $N_i$ the
addable-minus-removable count, proved to be the Cartan pairing in
[[lem-the-node-count-is-the-level-one-cartan-pairing]], and
$K_d|\lambda\rangle=q^{-m_0(\lambda)}|\lambda\rangle$.

A partition is **$e$-regular** if each positive part occurs with multiplicity
$<e$, and **$e$-restricted** if $\lambda_r-\lambda_{r+1}<e$ for every $r\ge1$
(with $\lambda_{r}=0$ beyond the length). These operators are declared linear
endomorphisms here; the affine relations proved later establish the actual
module structure, so nothing about $F$ is silently assumed in this Definition.

decreasing content, call a vertex state $+$ when the slot is occupied (addable)
and $-$ when it is empty (removable), so that the state word records the

coproduct and $K$-exponent $q^{\#+-\#-}$; in particular the raw $A_0$-partition
span is stable under the actual normalized string operators, $f$ applies to the
first surviving $+$ and $e$ to the last surviving $-$ in decreasing-content
order, equivalently $f$ to the last $+$ and $e$ to the first $-$ in

By [F1] the $K_i$ are diagonal in the partition basis and $F_j,E_j$ shift the weight by $\mp\alpha_j$; hence $K_iE_jK_i^{-1}=q^{\langle\alpha_j,h_i\rangle}E_j=q^{a_{ij}}E_j$ and $K_iF_jK_i^{-1}=q^{-a_{ij}}F_j$, the $K$'s commute, and the central product acts by $q$ by [F4].

The mixed commutators. Fix $i
e j$ and a partition $\lambda$. The two colors act on their own corner sets; restricting to the union of the $i$-cube and the $j$-cube through $\lambda$, the two operators move different corners or the same corner in different directions. If the moves commute (different corners) both orders give the same partition and the same product of exponents; if they obstruct each other (adjacent moves sharing a corner) both orders vanish, because the intermediate collision is a repeated-entry wedge; and no configuration produces a nonzero remainder, since the only corners whose availability can change are the two touched cells, whose residues $i
e j$ differ. Hence $[E_i,F_j]=0$ for $i
e j$ on every vector, while $[E_i,F_i]=(K_i-K_i^{-1})/(q-q^{-1})$ is the rank-one commutator of [F2].

By steps 1.1 and 2.1 the node operators satisfy every toral rule and every mixed commutator, and by [F2] each single-color action is integrable; the rank-one Serre engine [F3] then forces both quantum Serre sums for every pair $i\ne j$, the $e=2$ cubic case included. $U_q(\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}_e)$ with the fixed coproduct and the cyclic Cartan
datum: all toral commutation rules and mixed commutators

Let $\lambda\in P$ be a dominant integral label weight, put
$m_i:=\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle\ge0$, and let $M(\lambda)$ be the quantum Verma
module with highest vector $v_\lambda$
([[def-quantum-verma-module-and-simple-highest-weight-quotient]],
[[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]).

(i) The quotient $\tilde L(\lambda):=M(\lambda)/\sum_iU_q(\mathfrak g)F_i^{(m_i+1)}v_\lambda$
is nonzero, has finite-dimensional label weights and support
$\lambda-Q_+$, is integrable, and equals the canonical simple highest weight
module $L(\lambda)$, which is simple also as an ordinary (not assumed graded)
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module.

(ii) **Universality.** Every integrable cyclic highest weight module $V$ of
highest weight $\lambda$ with highest vector $v\ne0$ receives a
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module map $\tilde L(\lambda)\to V$ with
$\bar v_\lambda\mapsto v$, and this map is unique; every nonzero such $V$ is
isomorphic to $L(\lambda)$.

(iii) Its character equals the classical integrable highest weight character of
the explicitly regularized realization of the datum. No global
$\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-freeness and no crystal or global basis is used.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group
with $a_{ii}=2$ for all $i$
([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]), with root lattice $Q$,
simple roots $\alpha_i\in P$ and integer pairing
$\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle:P\times P^{\vee}\to\mathbb Z$, and let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra with generators $E_i,F_i,K_h$
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]). The lattice $P$ plays
the role of the integral weights of the classical theory
([[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]); the pairing need not
be perfect, and no identification $P=\operatorname{Hom}(P^{\vee},\mathbb Z)$ is
assumed anywhere.

A **$P$-graded type-one quantum weight module** is a left $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module $M$
together with a direct sum decomposition

$$M=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}M_\mu$$

(an internal direct sum of $\mathbb Q(q)$-subspaces, only finitely many nonzero
on each vector) such that, for all $\mu\in P$, $h\in P^{\vee}$ and $i\in I$,

$$K_h\ \text{acts on}\ M_\mu\ \text{by the scalar}\ q^{\langle\mu,h\rangle},\qquad E_iM_\mu\subseteq M_{\mu+\alpha_i},\qquad F_iM_\mu\subseteq M_{\mu-\alpha_i}.$$

The subspaces $M_\mu$ are the **chosen label-weight spaces**: the grading is
part of the structure and is not reconstructed from the action, because the
pairing may have a kernel. **Morphisms** of $P$-graded type-one weight modules
are the $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module maps $f\colon M\to N$ with
$f(M_\mu)\subseteq N_\mu$ for every $\mu$; the weight submodules and quotients
considered on this page are those with the induced grading (Verification, steps
3.1 and 4.1).

The module is **integrable** if $E_i$ and $F_i$ are locally nilpotent on every
vector: for every $v\in M$ and every $i$ there are integers $N_e(v,i),N_f(v,i)\ge1$
with $E_i^{N_e(v,i)}v=0$ and $F_i^{N_f(v,i)}v=0$. The exponents may depend on
the vector and on $i$, and both directions are required independently;
integrability is not a uniform nilpotence condition.

finiteness of the dimension of every $M_\mu$; boundedness of the set of $\mu$
with $M_\mu\ne0$ above (or below); finite generation of $M$. The zero module is
a $P$-graded type-one weight module with the empty grading ($M_\mu=0$ for all
$\mu$), and it is integrable.

separates $P$, the spaces $M_\mu$ are exactly the simultaneous eigenspaces of
the $K_h$, and the present definition recovers the usual type-one weight
modules (Verification, steps 2.1 and 4.1). Second, when the pairing does not
separate, distinct labels $\mu\ne\mu'$ may carry the same toral character, and
a simultaneous toral eigenspace must not be equated with a single label space;
the definition therefore takes the label grading as data. The regularization of
finite-cone support and all highest-weight comparisons on this page are proved
later, not assumed here by writing $P=\operatorname{Hom}(P^{\vee},\mathbb Z)$.
No choice principle enters this definition.

derivations.claim: The vacuum data. By [F1] the vacuum is killed by all $E_i$, is a $K_i$-eigenvector with eigenvalue $q^{\delta_{i0}}$ and a $K_d$-eigenvector with eigenvalue $1$, so $\mathrm{wt}(\varnothing)=\Lambda_0$ by the node-count pairing; in particular the vacuum is a highest weight vector of weight $\Lambda_0$.

Integrability and the highest-vector relations. The nonzero cyclic submodule $M=U_q|\varnothing\rangle$ inherits integrability and the label grading from $F$ by [F2]. Its generator has the highest-vector data of step 1.1, so it meets the integrable highest-vector hypothesis of [F3]. No assertion about the weight of a highest vector in an arbitrary submodule is needed.

Identification and the integral lattice. By [F3] the normalized assignment $v_0\mapsto|\varnothing\rangle$ extends to a homomorphism $V(\Lambda_0)\to M$. It is surjective since the image contains the cyclic generator, and injective since its kernel is a submodule of the simple source and the map is nonzero. Thus $M\cong V(\Lambda_0)$, which proves simplicity as well as the highest weight identification. The divided node operators preserve the partition Laurent lattice: on each finite two-vertex tensor cube this follows from the divided-power coproduct, whose tensor-factor divided powers are integral; hence $U_A^-|\varnothing\rangle$ is an $A$-submodule of that lattice, and it spans $M$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$ because ordinary lower words are scalar multiples of divided lower words. This is the claimed integral lattice.

Conclusion. The vacuum is a highest weight vector of weight $\Lambda_0$, its cyclic submodule is the simple integrable $V(\Lambda_0)$, and the crystal identification with the empty component of the good-node graph is postponed to the crystal theorem rather than asserted here.

The empty component consists of regular partitions. Use decreasing-content order and the survivor rule. If removing the selected last surviving minus creates $e$ equal rows of length $L-1$, then below its removable row there is a block of $e-1$ rows of length $L-1$ whose last corner is a consecutive same-residue minus: if the upper minus survives, so does this lower one, so the upper one cannot have been selected; hence good deletion preserves regularity. Dually, if adding the selected first surviving plus creates $e$ equal rows of the new length, then a block of $e-1$ rows of that length lies immediately above it and its first addable corner is a consecutive same-residue plus which survives whenever the lower plus does, so the lower plus is not selected; hence cogood addition preserves regularity. Both operators therefore stay inside the regular labels.

Reachability of all regular partitions and the component. Every nonempty regular partition has a top block of $a<e$ equal rows; its first removable corner has residue $L-a$, while the only earlier addable corner has residue $L$, so the minus has no matching same-residue plus and survives: a good deletion exists, it remains regular and lowers the size. Induction on the size together with the inverse axiom reaches every regular partition from the empty one, and since the empty partition is regular and all edges of the component preserve regularity, the empty component is exactly the set of $e$-regular partitions. The transposed ($e$-restricted) model arises by conjugation and is not the same vertex set.

Conclusion. The crystal basis of the whole Fock space is the good-node partition graph on all partitions with the survivor $\varepsilon,\varphi$, and its empty connected component is exactly the $e$-regular partition set, proved by the block argument without an imported path count or an abstract rank-one recognition.
